prompt:
ROLE INSTRUCTIONS
You are an EVALUATOR that infers latent behavioral signals from Slack-style corporate conversations.
You do NOT have access to the true scenario labels. You must infer using ONLY:
* trajectory_signature / the participant’s trajectory and summarized history (to calibrate vocabulary and context);
* the channel content and structure (messages + artifact_refs + decision_refs + thread_outcome).

CRITICAL OUTPUT RESTRICTIONS
* Return ONLY a single valid JSON object in the schema specified at the end.
* Do not include text outside the JSON.
* Do not use numbers (no score, no probability, no confidence).
* For each attribute, return ONLY one label in {LOW, MID, HIGH}.
* DETERMINISTIC RULE: if you are unsure/ambiguous, choose MID.
* Evidence snippets must be SHORT QUOTES from the text (no comments) and must NOT contain “LOW/MID/HIGH”.
* DO NOT use literal line breaks inside strings. If needed, use \n or if it is a tab use \t.
* Ensure quotes and braces are closed.

GLOSSARY (only for conceptual consistency; do NOT cite this in the output)
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions.

INPUT
* participants_json: list of participants, each with:
    {
        "_id": int,
        "role": string,                            # role of the participant
        "trajectory_lastK": [string],              # ESCO titles (short list, in chronological order)
        "trajectory_summary": string,              # consolidated summary (may contain “->”)
        "skills_text": string,                     # skills extracted from trajectory
    }
* channel: threads and messages (msg_id, speaker_id, reply_to, text, mentions, artifact_refs, decision_refs, reactions)
* (optional) thread_outcome per thread (decisions_made, next_steps)

IMPORTANT: You will use the participants' information [INPUT PARTICIPANTS] as a basis to try to infer the skill, productivity, and performance levels of each participant. Comparing the "resume/career path" with what can be observed in the "day-to-day" [INPUT CHANNEL] through the channel's messages. In other words, you can compare expectations (what is expected from the participant's career path and their position) with reality. Always evaluate participants in relation to the group, that is, within the group itself, who stands out the most, who stands out the least, and who is average, using the criteria of HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

DETERMINISTIC PROCEDURE (for each participant)
1. Collect candidate evidence:
   * Messages where speaker_id == the participant’s _id.
   * If the participant speaks little, you can also use messages that mention them (mentions contains _id) as contextual evidence.
2. For each attribute (productivity, ability, performance), mark:
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of HIGH => candidate HIGH
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of LOW  => candidate LOW
   * otherwise => MID
3. Attention:
   * If there are strong signals of HIGH and LOW at the same time for the same attribute, choose MID (conservative rule).
   * In the corporate context, everyone needs to deliver and demonstrate work; be careful to infer HIGH for something standard that should be MID.
   * Having one to four pieces of evidence for threads (<= 4 evidence items * threads) is not strong evidence.
4. Little evidence:
   * If there are no messages from the participant, use MID for all three attributes and use evidence from a message where they were mentioned.

EVIDENCE RULES (MANDATORY)
* For each participant, return 2 to 5 items in evidence.
* Each evidence item:
  * attribute ∈ {"productivity","ability","performance"}
  * msg_id must exist in the channel
  * justification: one sentence justifying the label.
  * snippet must be a short quote (up to ~20 words) copied from the text of that msg (no comment).
* Do not invent msg_id.
* Do not include “LOW/MID/HIGH” in the snippet.

OUTPUT FORMAT (OUTPUT JSON SCHEMA)
{
  "predictions": [
    {
      "_id": 0,
      "productivity_level": "LOW|MID|HIGH",
      "ability_level": "LOW|MID|HIGH",
      "performance_level": "LOW|MID|HIGH",
      "justification": "string",
      "evidence": [
        {"attribute": "productivity|ability|performance", "msg_id": "M12", "snippet": "..."}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
FINAL
Return only the JSON in the schema above.

          "text": "Good points on staff and visitor flows.\nProposal for standard access steps in A2 and T2:\nStaff:\n- Badge presented and validated at turnstile\n- Visual check that photo matches person\n- Random secondary questions during peak times (department or manager) at a defined rate\nVisitors:\n- Verify ID and visit purpose\n- Register in log with host or patient details\n- Issue visitor badge, must be visible at all times\n- Escort to restricted areas when required\nDeliveries:\n- Verify delivery documents\n- Register driver and company\n- Apply package-type specific checks (small parcels vs pallets) as 4001 suggested\nEvents:\n- Define light vs strict bag check mode based on event risk and expected crowd size\nIf we agree on this, we can treat it as the standard for A2 and T2.",

          "speaker_id": 13804,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "Switching to patrol routes in A2 and T3.\nDraft proposal:\nDay shift\n- Commercial: one full loop every 45 minutes, including all main entrances, side doors, and fire exits.\n- Parking: full sweep of all levels every 60 minutes, with extra focus on level -1 stairwell.\n- Hospital-like: corridor and treatment wing check every 30 minutes, including fire safety equipment.\n- Loading bay and mail room: check every 60 minutes, aligned with main delivery windows.\nNight shift\n- Commercial: full loop every 60 minutes, with extra checks on closed shop fronts and shutters.\n- Parking: full sweep every 45 minutes, focusing on loitering and vehicle security.\n- Hospital-like: 45-minute checks, quieter but still sensitive.\n- Loading bay and mail room: 90-minute checks, plus any time a delivery arrives.\nAll routes include checking fire extinguishers, alarms, and access points as per T3.\nPlease flag anything that is not realistic with current headcount or that misses key spots.",

I can help set up the string and check the levels while you place the bedding.\nWhere we switch to buried pipe, we will remove enough of the old channel to get a clean trench and proper bedding, but we will not chase the old concrete further than needed.         {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 70034,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "First asphalt delivery is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon, but the forecast shows possible rain showers.\nWe need to agree on clear go or no-go criteria for paving under these conditions and on the minimum compaction and surface checks we must complete before opening any section to traffic.\nA3 and A6 give us some guidance, and T6, T8, and T10 are directly affected.\nCan we define when we proceed with paving despite a marginal forecast, and what checks are non-negotiable before we let trucks use the new surface?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T6",
            "T8",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            6789,
            168084,
            192754,
            367549,
            384719
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 6789,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "From site this morning, the base looks good and ready for T6 on the first stretch.\nFor weather, I would be cautious about starting if there is a high chance of rain during paving or compaction. Wet surface or rain on hot mix will cause problems.\nMaybe we can set a rule that we only start if the forecast shows at least a few dry hours and the surface is dry, and we have covers ready for any open joints if a shower comes.\nOn checks, I think we should at least confirm mix temperature on arrival, layer thickness, and visual surface condition before opening.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 168084,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "For go or no-go, I suggest we use three checks: 1) no standing water on the base, 2) forecast shows at least a 3–4 hour dry window, and 3) air and surface temperature within the range recommended for the mix.\nIf any of these are not met, we should postpone paving and adjust A3 accordingly.\nBefore opening to traffic, we should complete compaction to the planned number of passes, check crossfall and smoothness, and do at least a basic friction check using the device we have.\nA6 can be used to record that all these checks are done for each section.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 192754,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "I will be helping with the paving crew.\nIf it starts to drizzle lightly while we are compacting, do we stop immediately or can we finish the passes on that short stretch?\nAlso, for T8, do we need any special checks on the roller or paver because of the wet conditions, or just the usual pre-start from A2?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034,
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 367549,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "From what I have seen before, even light rain can cause issues if it hits fresh asphalt.\nI think we should plan to stop paving if it starts raining and only finish compaction on what is already laid if the surface is not getting washed. But I would like 70034 to confirm.\nFor T8, I will make sure we do the usual pre-start checks from A2 and keep an eye on the water levels in the rollers so we do not over-wet the drums.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034,
            192754
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 384719,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "On the minimum checks before opening, I would add that we should walk the lane and look for any segregation, open joints, or visible roller marks.\nFor friction, we can use the measuring device and record the readings in A3 and A6 under T10.\nIf any section does not meet the basic friction or visual standard, we should keep it closed and either re-roll or repair before letting trucks through.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 70034,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "On light drizzle: if it starts raining while we are paving, we stop laying new mix immediately. If it is only a brief light drizzle and the surface is not getting washed, we can finish compaction on the area already laid, but we will need to inspect it carefully afterwards.\nFor T8, the usual pre-start checks from A2 are still valid. We just need to be extra careful with water on drums and make sure the paver and roller are not leaking fluids onto the mat.\nWe will not start paving if there is standing water or if the forecast shows heavy rain in the next couple of hours.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            192754,
            367549
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M62",
          "speaker_id": 6789,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "I support the three checks you listed for go or no-go.\nOn site, I can confirm the base is dry and free of standing water and check the surface temperature before we start T6.\nIf we decide to postpone, I will update A3 with the reason so it is clear why the production numbers changed.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M63",
          "speaker_id": 168084,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "Good addition.\nSo for minimum checks before opening, we will require: 1) full compaction passes completed, 2) crossfall and thickness checked, 3) friction reading taken and recorded, and 4) visual walkover to spot defects.\nWe can capture all of this in A6 and T10 for each section before we remove any barriers.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T10",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            384719
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M64",
          "speaker_id": 192754,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "Understood.\nI will be ready to stop feeding the paver as soon as we see rain starting and focus on finishing compaction on the laid area only if it is safe.\nFor T8, I will help with the pre-start checks and keep an eye out for any leaks or issues during paving.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M65",
          "speaker_id": 367549,
          "reply_to": "M63",
          "text": "I will handle the friction measurements and log them in A3 and A6 under T10.\nIf any reading looks low, I will flag it immediately so we can decide whether to re-roll or keep the section closed.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M66",
          "speaker_id": 384719,
          "reply_to": "M63",
          "text": "I will support with the visual walkover and crossfall checks before we open each lane.\nWe should also make sure the temporary signage from A4 is updated as soon as we switch traffic onto a new asphalt section.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M67",
          "speaker_id": 70034,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "Let me summarise the criteria so we can confirm them.\n1) Go or no-go for paving under marginal weather: we only start T6 if there is no standing water on the base, the forecast shows at least a 3–4 hour dry window, and air and surface temperatures are within the recommended range. If rain starts, we stop laying new mix immediately and only finish compaction on what is already down if the surface is not being washed.\n2) Minimum checks before opening to traffic: for each section we will complete full compaction passes, check thickness and crossfall, take and record friction readings, and do a visual walkover to spot defects. All of this will be recorded in A3 and A6 under T10 before we remove barriers.\nIf everyone is ok with this, we will use these as our standard for the paving phase.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            6789,
            168084,
            192754,
            367549,
            384719
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M68",
          "speaker_id": 6789,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "Aligned.\nI will check base and surface conditions on site before we start T6 and confirm whether we meet the go criteria, and I will help with the visual walkover before opening each section.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M69",
          "speaker_id": 168084,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "No objections.\nI will focus on ensuring the compaction passes and friction checks are completed and recorded in A6 and T10 before we open any lane to traffic.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M70",
          "speaker_id": 192754,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "Works for me.\nI will be ready to stop paving if the weather turns and will follow the instructions on when we can continue compaction.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M71",
          "speaker_id": 367549,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "All good.\nI will handle the friction measurements and help keep A3 and A6 updated for each paved section.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M72",
          "speaker_id": 384719,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "Agreed.\nI will support with the visual checks and make sure the temporary signage is adjusted as we open new sections.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        }
      ],

      "thread_id": "TH5",
      "messages": [
        {
          "msg_id": "M73",
          "speaker_id": 6789,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Last paving section is now complete and cooling.\nWe are moving into close-out: permanent signage, markings, guardrails, and final inspections before we reopen full access.\nWe need to confirm that the permanent signage and guardrails planned in A4 and installed under T7 will be enough for reopening, and decide which minor items, if any, we can safely defer and capture in T11.\nA6 and A8 will also come into play for final checks and the drone survey.\nCan we align on what must be done before reopening and what can be scheduled after, without affecting safety or compliance?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A6",
            "A8",
            "T7",
            "T11",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034,
            168084,
            192754,
            367549,
            384719
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M74",
          "speaker_id": 168084,
          "reply_to": "M73",
          "text": "From the walkthrough I did this morning, most of the permanent signs and guardrails under T7 are already in place according to A4.\nFor reopening, I think we must have: 1) all regulatory and warning signs installed, 2) guardrails and toeboards in high-risk areas, 3) basic road markings at the junctions and lane edges, and 4) any missing signposts at least temporarily marked and protected.\nAnything that affects driver guidance or protection should not be deferred.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T7",
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            6789
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M75",
          "speaker_id": 70034,
          "reply_to": "M73",
          "text": "I agree with that list.\nLooking at A4, the critical items for reopening are the speed limit signs, warning signs near the yard entrance, and the guardrails along the drop-off. These must be fully installed and checked under T7 and A6.\nItems that might be candidates for deferral could be some non-critical road markings, extra directional arrows, or cosmetic touch-ups, as long as we clearly list them in T11 with due dates.\nWe should also plan the drone survey under T12 using A8 after reopening to confirm there are no missed items.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A6",
            "A8",
            "T7",
            "T11",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M76",
          "speaker_id": 192754,
          "reply_to": "M73",
          "text": "I helped install some of the guardrails under T7.\nI noticed a couple of short gaps where we are waiting for extra posts. For reopening, do we need to close those gaps with temporary barriers, or can we leave them open if they are short?\nAlso, for T12, I can help set up the safety perimeter for the drone flight, but I am not sure which exact areas we want to capture.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T7",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            70034,
            6789
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M77",
          "speaker_id": 367549,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "For the guardrail gaps, I think we should not leave any unprotected drop-offs when we reopen.\nIf the permanent posts are not in yet, we should use temporary barriers or toeboards and mark them clearly until we can finish T7.\nFor the drone survey under T12, I suggest we focus on the full 500 m stretch, especially the drainage edges and the areas near the yard entrance where traffic is heaviest.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T7",
            "T12",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            192754
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M78",
          "speaker_id": 384719,
          "reply_to": "M74",
          "text": "I walked the signs and markings as well.\nAll the main regulatory signs from A4 are in place, but a few directional arrows and some edge lines are still missing.\nI think we can reopen with the current markings if we add temporary cones or paint to highlight the lane edges, and then complete the remaining markings within a short time window after reopening. We should list those in T11 as deferred items.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T7",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            168084
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M79",
          "speaker_id": 6789,
          "reply_to": "M76",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.

* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 337175,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Quick update on API integration and security for the MVP.\n\nFor T3 and T6:\n- Ticketing sandbox: basic connectivity is working, ticketSearch and ticketCreate are returning data\n- Knowledge base: initial data model is in place, and a simple search endpoint is running in the test environment\n\nI have logged two issues in A8:\n1) Ticketing API rate limits are lower than expected\n2) Telephony system API requires additional authentication steps\n\nOn security (T8 and A4), I have started a draft checklist covering authentication, authorisation, logging, and data protection, but we need to agree on:\n- Which ticketing and telephony integrations are in scope for MVP\n- How strict we want to be on logging and audit trails in the first release\n\nWould like to use this thread to make those calls and then finalise A4.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T3",
            "T6",

            "T10"

          "decision_refs": [],

        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 109718,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "Thanks for the update.\n\nOn integration scope for MVP, my suggestion is:\n- Ticketing: full integration for search and creation via T3 (sandbox now, production later)\n- Telephony: keep it minimal for MVP, just enough to identify the caller and maybe open the dashboard with a parameter\n\nGiven the rate limits and extra auth steps you mentioned in A8, I would avoid deep telephony integration in the first 21 days.\n\nOn logging and audit trails, I think we should follow A4 as closely as we can, but if something is too heavy for MVP, we should at least have a clear plan to add it before broader rollout.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T3",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            337175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 561396,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "From the front-end side, we can support a light telephony integration by:\n- Accepting a caller identifier as a URL parameter\n- Using that to pre-fill the search field on the agent dashboard\n\nThis keeps T4 and T11 simple and avoids tight coupling to the telephony system for now.\n\nAnything beyond that (like full screen-pop flows) feels risky within the MVP timeline.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T4",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            337175,
            377231
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 6869,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "From the agent perspective, a light telephony integration is fine for the pilot.\n\nIf the call comes in and the dashboard opens with the caller id already in the search box, that is already a big improvement.\n\nWe do not need full call control in the portal for the first round, as long as the workflow is stable and does not slow us down.",
          "artifact_refs": [],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            109718,
            337175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 337175,
          "reply_to": "M36",
          "text": "That aligns with what I am seeing technically.\n\nFor MVP, I propose we define integration scope as:\n- Ticketing: search and create via T3, fully wired to sandbox and then production\n- Telephony: URL-based handoff with caller identifier only, no deep integration\n\nI will document this in A3 and A8 so it is clear what is in and out.\n\nIf we agree, we can treat this as the official MVP integration scope.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A8",
            "T3",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [

            561396,
            377231,
            6869

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 377231,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "Works for me. On the web side, that means we just need to:\n- Read the caller identifier from the URL\n- Trigger a search on page load if it is present\n\nNo extra UI complexity for T4 or T11 beyond that.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T4",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            337175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 109718,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "Agreed on the integration scope.\n\nOn the security checklist in A4 for T8, can you outline the main items you have so far? I want to make sure we are covering the basics required by ICT security legislation without overcomplicating the MVP.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            337175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 337175,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "Current draft of A4 for T8 includes:\n- Authentication: single sign-on for agents, separate login for customers\n- Authorisation: role-based access (agent vs customer vs content editor)\n- Logging: record login events, ticket view and update actions, and admin changes\n- Data protection: HTTPS everywhere, no sensitive data in URLs, basic data retention notes\n\nI still need to:\n- Align the checklist with the latest internal ICT security guidelines\n- Schedule an early review with the security contact\n\nFor MVP, I suggest we treat these items as mandatory, and anything beyond (like advanced anomaly detection) as post-MVP.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            109718
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 561396,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "From the front-end side, this is all doable for MVP:\n- We can ensure all calls go over HTTPS\n- We can avoid putting sensitive data in URLs\n- We can surface clear session timeout messages so agents are not surprised\n\nFor logging, we will rely on backend events, but we can make sure we send enough context (user id, ticket id) with each call.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T4",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            337175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 6869,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "On the agent side, the only thing I would flag is session timeouts.\n\nIf the portal logs us out too aggressively, it will hurt call handling time. As long as the timeout is reasonable and clearly communicated, the rest of the checklist sounds fine.",
          "artifact_refs": [],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [

            561396

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 109718,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "This looks like a solid baseline.\n\nI suggest we:\n- Finalise A4 with these items as mandatory for MVP\n- Mark anything else as 'next iteration' so we do not lose track\n\nWe will still need the internal security officer to sign off, but as a team we can treat this checklist as our go-live baseline.",

          "speaker_id": 337175,

          "text": "Agreed.\n\nI will:\n- Update A4 to clearly mark the MVP baseline items\n- Add a short 'post-MVP' section for advanced controls\n- Share A4 with the internal security contact for early feedback\n\nFrom our side, we can consider this checklist as the baseline for go-live readiness, pending that external review.",

          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Starting a thread on the pilot plan, training, and feedback.\n\nI have a first draft of the pilot training plan and quick-start guide in progress for T9.\n\nOutline so far in A2 and A6:\n- Training agenda: portal overview, agent dashboard walkthrough, top 10 scripts from T5, hands-on practice\n- Quick-start guide: screenshots of the main flows, plus a one-page cheat sheet\n- Governance: who owns knowledge base updates and how often we review content (based on A6)\n\nWe need to agree on:\n1) Pilot start date\n2) Which agent group will participate\n3) How we will collect and prioritise feedback (T12, A7)\n\nSharing this now so we can lock those decisions and adjust T7, T9, T11, and T12 accordingly.",

          "text": "Thanks for kicking this off.\n\nGiven the 21-day MVP window and current progress on T1–T4 and T3/T6/T10, I think a realistic pilot start date is the beginning of week 4, right after we have a few days of internal testing.\n\nProposal:\n- Finish core development and basic testing by end of day on day 18\n- Use days 19–20 for internal dry runs\n- Start the pilot with a small group of agents on day 21\n\nDoes that align with what you need for T9 and T12?",

          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 377231,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "From the web side, that timeline is tight but doable if we keep scope stable.\n\nT4 and T11 should be in a good enough state for training by day 18, assuming no major surprises from integration.\n\nWe will need at least one day to fix any usability issues that come out of the internal dry runs, but we can do that in parallel with finalising the quick-start guide.",

          "speaker_id": 337175,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "Backend is on track for that schedule as well.\n\nT3, T6, and T10 should be stable enough for a pilot by day 18, with logging and basic monitoring in place.\n\nWe will keep A8 updated with any issues that might affect the pilot so we can decide quickly whether to fix or work around them.",

          "text": "That timeline works for training.\n\nFor T9, I can:\n- Run a 2-hour training session with the pilot group on day 20\n- Use the quick-start guide as a handout\n- Do a short follow-up Q and A on day 21 after the first live calls\n\nOn the pilot group, I suggest:\n- 8–10 agents from different shifts\n- Mix of experienced and newer agents\n\nI can coordinate with the support manager to confirm names and shifts and record them under T9 in A3.",

          "text": "On the quick-start guide, if you share a draft of A2 with screenshots, I can help make sure the images match the latest UI from T4 and T11.\n\nWe should freeze the guide layout a couple of days before training so we are not chasing last-minute UI tweaks.",

          "text": "On T7, we will make sure the knowledge base management UI is ready for support staff before the pilot:\n- Editors can create, edit, publish, and archive articles\n- Role-based access is enforced\n\nThis ties into A6 so that the governance rules are actually enforceable in the tool.",

          "text": "We also need to agree on how we will collect and prioritise pilot feedback for T12.\n\nProposal:\n- Use A7 as the central feedback log\n- Collect feedback via a short survey after the first week plus a few quick interviews\n- For each item in A7, tag it as 'usability', 'bug', or 'feature request'\n- At the end of the pilot, identify the top 5 improvement items and feed them back into A3 for the next iteration\n\nDoes that sound workable?",

        {

          "reply_to": "M59",

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.

          "text": "On shelf filling:\n- For dairy and chilled drinks, I usually pull the trolley from the back corridor, park it at the end of the aisle, then work section by section.\n- I try to rotate stock, but when the trolley is mixed it is hard to find the oldest dates quickly.\n- Labels and prices: I change labels when I notice a mismatch, but there is no fixed moment in the routine.\nPain points:\n- Trolleys sometimes arrive half full of unrelated items, so I waste time sorting.\n- In the evening shift, we often get last-minute pallets that we cannot finish before closing.\nI agree dairy and chilled drinks could be a good pilot aisle, but we need to be careful with food safety and shelf life checks.",
          "artifact_refs": [],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [

            37492

        {

          "speaker_id": 331660,
          "reply_to": "M1",
          "text": "From the office side:\n- I receive the delivery paperwork, check against the system, and then note which pallets go to which aisles.\n- Right now, the mapping from pallets to aisles is quite rough, and we do not log where delays happen.\n- Stock counts for the aisle are done once a day, but not always at the same time.\nPain points:\n- When replenishment is late, the system still shows stock available, so we get customer complaints.\n- We do not have a clear view of which shift caused a delay.\nFor T1, I will map the current steps from truck unloading to shelf filling for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle, using your inputs. That will become the updated A1.\nOn pilot scope, I suggest we include all dairy and chilled drinks products in that aisle, both branded and own label, so we see enough volume but still keep it manageable.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M5",
          "speaker_id": 300804,
          "reply_to": "M1",
          "text": "Adding what I see from the desk:\n- I log delivery times and sometimes note if a pallet is damaged, but I do not always record which aisle it was for.\n- For the dairy aisle, I usually get calls from the floor when there are gaps, then I check the system and confirm stock is in the back.\n- There is no standard way to record these exceptions yet.\nI can help fill out forms and keep the workflow doc updated once we agree the exact steps for T1.",

            "T1"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M6",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M2",
          "text": "Thanks for the detail on loading and movement.\nFollow-up questions:\n- When you say pallets are overloaded, is that mainly on dairy and chilled drinks, or across all categories?\n- How often do you mix chilled with ambient on the same trolley for that aisle?\nThis will help when we design the standard sequence later for T2 and link it to the shift plan in A6.",

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            36271
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M7",
          "speaker_id": 36271,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "Overloaded pallets happen mostly on dairy and chilled drinks, especially on the first delivery of the week.\nMixing chilled with ambient on the same trolley for that aisle happens maybe half the time, usually when we are short on trolleys or in a rush.\nIf we fix the loading sequence in T2, I think we can keep chilled together and avoid stacking too high.",

            "T2"

          "mentions": [
            37492

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M8",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M3",
          "text": "On the shelf side, your point about mixed trolleys is important.\nFor the current workflow map in A1, I will note that sorting is happening at the aisle instead of in the backroom.\nCan you confirm roughly how long it takes you to fill the full dairy and chilled drinks aisle on a normal delivery, and how that changes on evening shifts?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            321832
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M9",
          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M8",
          "text": "On a normal morning delivery, filling the full dairy and chilled drinks aisle takes about 90 minutes if the trolley is well organised.\nIf the trolley is mixed and I have to sort a lot, it can go up to 2 hours.\nOn evening shifts, it is similar, but we lose time when customers are in the way and when we get late pallets close to closing time.",
          "artifact_refs": [],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M10",
          "speaker_id": 331660,
          "reply_to": "M4",
          "text": "I can support with T6 once T1 and A1 are drafted.\nMy idea is to:\n- Split the dairy and chilled drinks aisle into clear sections for each shift.\n- Assign movers and shelf fillers per section and time slot, so we avoid everyone arriving at once.\n- Add a simple rotation so the same person is not always on the heaviest section.\nI will sketch a first version of A6 after we lock the pilot aisle and start date.",

        {

          "reply_to": "M4",
          "text": "So far, everyone seems aligned on using the dairy and chilled drinks aisle as the pilot area, covering all products in that aisle.\nUnless there are strong objections, I suggest we confirm that as our pilot scope for D1.\nOn timing: given the 21-day limit, I propose we start next Monday, run the pilot for the full 21 days, and do a mid-pilot review at the end of week one.\nDoes that work for day and evening shifts?",

          "text": "Starting next Monday works for me.\nFor evenings, I suggest we avoid testing big changes on Friday and Saturday nights, as those are busier.\nWe can still follow the new routine, but maybe keep some flexibility those days.\nI am fine confirming the dairy and chilled drinks aisle as the pilot area.",

          "msg_id": "M17",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "As agreed, here is the first draft of the new loading and movement sequence and the shelf replenishment routine for the dairy and chilled drinks aisle.\nLoading and movement (draft A2, from T2):\n- Separate pallets by aisle and by temperature zone in the backroom.\n- Build trolleys so chilled dairy and chilled drinks are together, heavier items at the bottom, lighter on top, within equipment capacity.\n- Limit trolley height so movers can see over the load.\n- Move trolleys to the aisle in smaller batches to avoid blocking.\nShelf replenishment routine (draft A4, from T4):\n- Start with checking dates and rotating stock, then fill from back to front.\n- Check labels and prices as you go, correcting any mismatches.\n- Keep the aisle clear for customers and cleaning.\nPlease review and comment. We need to agree on the final versions for D3 and D4 before Monday.",

          "speaker_id": 36271,
          "reply_to": "M17",
          "text": "On the loading side, this looks doable.\nQuestions:\n- For separating pallets by temperature zone, do we have enough space in the backroom to keep chilled dairy and chilled drinks apart from ambient?\n- For trolley height, can we set a simple rule, like not higher than my shoulders, so it is easy to follow?\nI like the idea of smaller batches to avoid blocking, but we will need to coordinate with cleaning for T10 so we do not clash in the corridor.",

          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M17",
          "text": "On the shelf routine:\n- Starting with date checks and rotation is good, but we should be clear on how to handle short-dated items we cannot fit on the shelf.\n- For labels and prices, can we add a step to check the promo section separately? That is where I see most mismatches.\n- We should also define how many sections we aim to complete before we move the trolley, so we do not leave it blocking the aisle.\nOverall, the structure in A4 makes sense to me.",

We can write it into A2 as 'do not stack higher than shoulder level of the mover using the trolley'.\nOn T10, I will speak with the cleaning and maintenance coordinator so we can align cleaning times with the new movement sequence and avoid blocked aisles.",

          "text": "For the shelf routine, I can help by preparing a simple printed version of A4 that shelf fillers can keep on the trolley.\nI just need the final steps confirmed for T4.\nAlso, should we add a note about where to put empty packaging and waste so it does not block the aisle?",

            321832

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M22",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "Good points on short-dated items and promos.\nProposal to update A4:\n- After date checks, if we find short-dated items that do not fit on the shelf, we place them in a clearly marked short-date section in the chiller and inform the duty manager.\n- Add a specific step to check promo labels and prices at the end of each section.\n- Define that the trolley should be parked at the end of the aisle or in a bay that does not block customers while we work on a section.\nWould that cover your concerns for T4?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            321832
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M23",
          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "Yes, that works for me.\nOne more detail: can we specify that we always pull older stock forward before adding new, even if it means taking a bit longer on busy days?\nThat will help with food safety and reduce waste.",

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492

          "msg_id": "M24",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M23",
          "text": "Agreed. I will add a clear line in A4 that we always pull older stock forward before placing new items, even on busy days, unless a manager explicitly instructs otherwise.\nThat will also link nicely with the safety and hygiene checklist in A3 later.",

            321832

        },
        {

          "speaker_id": 36271,
          "reply_to": "M20",
          "text": "The floor markings in the backroom will help.\nFor the loading sequence in A2, can we also say:\n- Put the heaviest crates at the bottom, then medium, then light.\n- Keep liquids low so they do not crush softer items.\nI want to be sure we stay within the lifting equipment capacity and avoid strain.",

          "mentions": [

            37492

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M26",
          "speaker_id": 331660,
          "reply_to": "M25",
          "text": "Yes, we can add those rules into A2.\nI will also include a reminder to check the trolley and pallet capacity labels before loading, so we do not exceed limits.\nOnce we finalise the text, we should run T7 on two delivery days to test the new sequence and log any issues.",

          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M18",
          "text": "On your earlier question about space: I checked the backroom layout.\nWe can create two marked zones for chilled dairy and chilled drinks without moving any fixed structures.\nWe will need to keep those zones clear of other stock, so I will add that as a note in A2.\nIf we see that it is not working during T7, we can adjust.",

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M28",
          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M21",
          "text": "On empty packaging and waste, I suggest we:\n- Flatten cardboard and place it on the bottom of the trolley once a section is done.\n- Put plastic wrap and small waste in a bag attached to the trolley.\n- Take all waste back to the backroom at the end of the aisle before moving to the next section.\nWe can add this to A4 so it is part of the routine.",

          "msg_id": "M29",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M28",
          "text": "Good addition. I will include the waste handling steps in A4.\nWe should also make sure T10 reflects that cleaning will not start in the aisle until waste is cleared and trolleys are parked in the agreed spots.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M17",
          "text": "Based on the feedback, I have updated A2 and A4 with:\n- Clear loading rules on weight distribution, trolley height and temperature zones.\n- Movement in smaller batches with marked backroom zones and agreed parking spots.\n- Shelf routine steps for rotation, short-dated items, promo checks, waste handling and keeping aisles clear.\nUnless there are any last-minute concerns today, I propose we approve these as the standard loading and movement sequence and shelf replenishment routine for the pilot (D3 and D4), and use them from Monday.\nWe will still be able to fine-tune after the first week if needed.",

          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Sharing the draft safety and hygiene checklist and the incident and exception log for the pilot.\nSafety and hygiene checklist (draft A3, from T3 and linked to T12):\n- Check PPE and safe lifting posture before starting.\n- Confirm trolley and pallet loads are within capacity and not stacked above shoulder height.\n- For dairy and chilled drinks, check temperatures, packaging integrity and dates before filling.\n- Ensure rotation is done correctly and short-dated items are handled as agreed.\nIncident and exception log (draft A7, from T9):\n- Simple form to record damaged goods, missing items, unsafe situations, delays and any hygiene issues.\n- Fields: date, time, aisle, product, description, who reported, immediate action.\nPlease review and comment. We need to confirm the final checklist (D5) and agree when and how to fill in the log (D6) before the pilot starts.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T3",
            "T12",
            "A7",
            "T9"
          ],

          "mentions": [

            300804

        {
          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 36271,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "On the checklist for movers:\n- I like the reminder about trolley capacity and height.\n- Could we add a quick step to check the floor for spills or obstacles before moving a loaded trolley?\nFor the incident log, I am ok filling it in, but I will need a clear example of what counts as an incident versus something we just fix on the spot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "From the shelf side:\n- The checklist items on rotation and dates look good.\n- I suggest we add a line to check that chilled doors close properly and are not blocked by trolleys or boxes.\nOn the incident log, I think we should log any case where we have to remove products from sale due to date or temperature issues, not just physical damage.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 331660,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "Good point on spills and obstacles.\nI will add a step in A3 for movers to check the floor and clear any hazards before moving a loaded trolley.\nOn what counts as an incident in A7, my suggestion:\n- Log anything that could affect safety, product quality or customer experience, even if you fix it.\n- Examples: near misses with trolleys, repeated delays, products found out of temperature, damaged packaging, or missing items.\nWe can include a short example list at the top of the form.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            36271,
            37492
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 300804,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "I can help by keeping the A7 log file up to date.\nQuestion on T9: who should be responsible for entering the incidents, the person who sees it or the office?\nMaybe we can say that movers and shelf fillers note the basics on paper during the shift, and I enter them into A7 at the end of the day.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A7",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492,
            331660
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 37492,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "For T9 and D6, I like the split you suggest.\nProposal:\n- Whoever spots the incident (mover or shelf filler) fills a short paper slip during the shift.\n- At the end of the day, office staff consolidate all slips into the digital A7 log.\n- If there is a serious safety or hygiene issue, the person who spots it must also call the duty manager immediately, not wait for the log.\nWe can also link this to T12 so the health and safety officer can review non-compliance cases.",

            "A7",

            "D6"

          "speaker_id": 321832,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "That process works for me.\nFor timing, should we say that we fill the paper slip as soon as we can after the incident, ideally within the same hour, so we do not forget details?",

            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            37492
          ]

          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 36271,

          "text": "I am ok with filling a paper slip when something happens.\nIt would help to have the slips stored near the back door so we can grab them quickly.\nOn the checklist A3, can we also remind movers to keep hands clear of pinch points when turning trolleys in tight spaces?",

          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M37",
          "text": "For late shift, the new pedestrian lane in A6 will help.\nSometimes people cut across the forklift path to get to the compactor.\nIf we put clear tape and signs, that should guide them.\nOn rotation, I am ok with swapping between picking and baler feeding as shown in A8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M37",
          "text": "From a recycling and hazardous handling view, moving the hazardous cage entrance away from the main forklift turn is a big improvement.\nWe just need to keep enough space for the blue drum and other containers inside.\nOn the cleaning list in A4, I suggest we add a quick visual check that hazardous labels are still readable and containers are closed before we start washing floors nearby.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Good catch.\nI will update A6 to mark a no-parking zone at that turn and add a line in A4: 'Check that no pallets or bins are parked in the marked forklift turn area'.\nOn rotation, I will adjust A8 so no one stays at the compactor more than one hour in a row, as suggested for T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T6",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            307206,
            204917
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M40",
          "text": "On the cleaning steps, I can help detail which products to use where.\nFor T6, we can say:\n- neutral detergent for general floor cleaning.\n- no bleach or strong acids near the hazardous cage.\n- use absorbent granules for spills.\nWe can add that to A4 with simple icons.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M44",
          "text": "Yes, that matches what we already use.\nIf we list it clearly in A4, it will help new staff.\nI can test the updated checklist on night shift for T6 and note any issues.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            204917
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 307206,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "With the no-parking zone and the clearer path in A6, I am comfortable with the new forklift route.\nAs long as the markings are bright and we keep them in A4 checks, it should stay clear.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "I am ok with the new layout too.\nThe pedestrian lane and no-parking zone will make it easier to see where to walk and where not to leave bins.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "From early shift, the updated A6 looks good.\nNo issues with emergency exits or clearances.\nI am fine to confirm this layout for the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "Agree with the others.\nThe new layout in A6 improves both safety and flow in the pilot area.\nI am ok to lock it in and share with the shift supervisor and maintenance for final checks.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M49",
          "text": "Great, we will treat the updated A6 as the agreed layout and forklift paths for the pilot area.\nI will send it to the shift supervisor and maintenance for their sign-off under T4.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            307206,
            204917,
            31940,
            468833,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "On the rotation plan in A8, I have now:\n- 1 hour at first pick station.\n- 1 hour at second pick station.\n- 1 hour at compactor area.\n- 1 hour on lighter duties (baler feeding, housekeeping, checklist checks).\nThen repeat.\nThis covers a full shift with breaks.\nAny concerns with coverage of key positions for T12?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            204917,
            31940,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "That pattern works for early shift.\nWe just need to make sure someone is always available to do the A2 load check before starting a new batch.\nMaybe we can assign that to whoever is on lighter duties in A8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "For late shift, I am ok with that rotation.\nHaving a lighter block after compactor duty will help.\nNo gaps that I can see.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "Night shift can follow the same pattern.\nDuring the lighter block we can also do the cleaning checks from A4.\nThat way the checklist is not forgotten.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "Sounds good.\nWe will use A8 as the standard rotation schedule for the pilot, with the lighter block covering A2 load checks and A4 cleaning checks.\nNow on the cleaning routine itself: the updated A4 has tasks split by time of day (start, mid-shift, end) and includes PPE and products.\nWe also need to agree who signs it off each shift.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T6",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            204917,
            31940,
            489662,
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "I suggest the person on lighter duties at the end of the shift does the final walk-through and signs A4, but the shift supervisor should also initial it when they do their round.\nThat way it is clear who checked what.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "Agree.\nOperator signs A4 for the tasks they completed, and the shift supervisor initials once they have verified the area.\nThis keeps it simple but still accountable.\nFrom my side, the content of A4 now covers what we need for T6.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "I am ok with that.\nI can sign A4 on night shift and ask the supervisor to initial during their round.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "Same for late shift.\nHappy to sign the checklist when I am on the lighter block.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "Ok, we will lock A4 as the daily cleaning and inspection routine for the pilot area, with the operator on lighter duties signing and the shift supervisor initialling.\nI will finalise A6, A8 and A4 and share them for printing so we can start the pilot.",

          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted the hazardous waste handling and storage guide for the sorting area (A3) and a quick reference for incident and near-miss reporting (A5).\nThese are linked to T5, T7 and also touch T9 for collection timing.\nThe hazardous guide lists common items we see: batteries, aerosols, paint tins, chemicals, electronics, and how to drain, store and label them.\nThe incident sheet explains when to report, who to call, and how to use the simple card.\nPlease review and flag anything that does not match what you see on the line.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A5",
            "T5",
            "T7",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            31940,
            204917,
            307206,
            41356,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M62",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "On A3, the section about draining paint tins says to drain into the red drum.\nCan we clarify that only if the label is readable and we know what it is?\nSometimes we get unlabelled containers.\nIn those cases I think we should not open them on the line.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M63",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "On A5, the incident examples are clear, but could we add one for a near miss with a forklift in the pilot area?\nPeople see those often but do not always report them.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M64",
          "speaker_id": 307206,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "Agree with adding a forklift near-miss example.\nAlso, on A3, for batteries, can we say clearly that they go straight into the yellow battery box and never into general scrap?\nI still see them mixed in sometimes.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M65",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "I like the pictures in A3.\nOne question: for small electronics like phones, do we treat them as hazardous or just as e-waste?\nMaybe we can add a simple rule there.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M66",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "On A5, the steps say to fill in a card and hand it to the supervisor.\nSometimes the supervisor is not on the floor.\nShould we also allow dropping the card in a box near the pilot area so it does not get lost?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M67",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M62",
          "text": "Good points.\nI will update A3 so that:\n- only labelled paint or chemical containers are opened and drained into the red drum.\n- unlabelled or damaged containers are placed in a sealed over-drum and flagged to the supervisor.\n- batteries always go into the yellow battery box, never into scrap.\nFor small electronics, we can say: 'phones, tablets and similar go into the e-waste crate, not general waste'.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356,
            307206,
            31940
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M68",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M63",
          "text": "On A5, I will add a forklift near-miss example: 'forklift brakes suddenly to avoid a person or bin in the path, even if no one is hit'.\nI will also add a line about the card box near the pilot area so people can drop cards there if the supervisor is not around.\nSupervisor will empty the box each shift.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            204917,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M69",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "The updated rules in A3 sound safe and practical.\nWe just need to make sure the over-drum is clearly marked and placed where the forklift can reach it without blocking the path.\nWe can align that with the layout in A6 and the collection schedule in T9 so it gets emptied regularly.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833,
            307206
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M70",
          "speaker_id": 307206,
          "reply_to": "M69",
          "text": "If we put the over-drum just inside the hazardous cage, I can pick it up with the forklift without blocking the main path.\nWe should note that in A3 and in the collection timing under T9 so it is cleared at least once a week.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            41356,
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M71",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M68",
          "text": "The incident steps in A5 are clear now.\nFor the pilot area, I suggest we keep it to three simple actions:\n1) Make the area safe.\n2) Tell the supervisor or call the number on the sheet.\n3) Fill in a card and hand it in or drop it in the box.\nAnything more and people might skip it.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M72",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "I like those three steps.\nEasy to remember.\nWe can also use them in the toolbox talk later.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            204917,
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M73",
          "speaker_id": 31940,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "With the pictures and simple rules in A3, I feel more confident about what to do with batteries, aerosols and phones.\nNo extra questions from me.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M74",
          "speaker_id": 41356,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "So to summarise:\n- A3 now lists common hazardous items, where they go, and special rules for labelled vs unlabelled containers.\n- A5 has three simple reporting steps plus examples, including forklift near misses.\nFrom my side, A3 is ready to use in the pilot area.\nWe will still ask the health and safety officer to review it formally, but I am comfortable treating this as our agreed guide.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A5",
            "T5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            468833,
            204917,
            307206,
            31940,
            489662
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M75",
          "speaker_id": 204917,
          "reply_to": "M74",
          "text": "I agree.\nThe hazardous guide in A3 is clear enough for all shifts.\nWe can walk through it quickly during the pilot start.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356,
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M76",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "On the incident process, I am happy to lock the three steps you listed as the standard for the sorting line:\n1) Make safe.\n2) Tell supervisor or call the number.\n3) Fill and hand in or drop a card.\nWe will put that wording on A5 and use it in T7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            204917
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M77",
          "speaker_id": 489662,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "Works for me.\nI will start using those three steps on night shift and encourage others to do the same.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M78",
          "speaker_id": 307206,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "Same here.\nIf we keep A5 posted near the pilot area, it will be easy to follow.\nI will also mention it on the radio when we have a near miss.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            468833
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M79",
          "speaker_id": 468833,
          "reply_to": "M74",
          "text": "I will finalise A3 and A5 with these updates and send them to the health and safety officer for formal review.\nIn parallel, we can start using them in the pilot area so we do not lose time.\nI will also check with logistics on T9 to make sure hazardous collections match the new storage setup.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A5",
            "T5",
            "T7",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            41356,

          ]
