        {
          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 107378,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "Thanks for setting this up.\nI propose we use the next monthly payroll cycle as the pilot, not the current one, so we have enough time to brief office clerks and finalise A4 and A5.\nFor success criteria, I suggest: all steps in A4 completed on time, all inputs logged in A2 using the new routing rules, and any issues captured in A7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A5",
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            408577,
            319449
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 421608,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "I agree that we should not use the current cycle, as deadlines are tight.\nUsing the next monthly cycle gives us time to align invoice issuing in T10 with the new document workflow as well.\nFor success, I would add that reconciliations should match without extra manual work, and that any discrepancies follow the escalation path in A8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A8",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            408577,
            107378
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 319449,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "From the office side, the next monthly cycle works.\nWe can use the time before then to walk through the routing rules in T4, the templates in T2, and the quick reference guide A6 with clerks.\nFor success, I would like to see that all forms in the pilot period are handled using the new routing and that clerks feel comfortable with the process.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T4",
            "T2",
            "A6",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            330756
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 330756,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "I am ok with using the next cycle.\nI will need a short walkthrough of the tracking sheet in T5 and how to log items in A2, but once I see it in action I should be fine.\nNo concerns on timing from me.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            319449
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 408577,
          "reply_to": "M49",
          "text": "So far, everyone seems aligned on using the next monthly cycle.\nUnless there are objections, we can record that as D7.\nFor success criteria under D8, I like the points mentioned: checklist completion, proper use of A2, reconciliations without extra manual work, and issues logged in A7.\nWe should also track how many urgent items miss the cut off, to see if the routing rules are realistic.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A4",
            "A7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            107378,
            421608,
            319449,
            330756
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 107378,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "Agreed on D7.\nFor D8, I suggest we define success as:\n- 100 percent of steps in A4 completed and ticked off in T5.\n- All payroll related forms in the pilot period logged in A2 with correct fields.\n- All discrepancies handled using the escalation path in A8 and recorded in A7.\n- No breaches of the confidentiality rules in A5.\nIf we meet these, we can consider the pilot successful and move to full rollout.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T5",
            "A2",
            "A8",
            "A7",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            408577,
            421608
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 421608,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "Those criteria work for me.\nOn T10, I will map the touchpoints between invoices and payroll before the pilot starts, so that any invoice related items are also tracked in A2 and archived according to A3.\nThis will help us see the full picture when we review the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A2",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            107378,
            408577
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 319449,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "I am aligned on D7 and D8.\nBefore the pilot, I will finalise the training outline in T12 and run a short session with clerks to walk through T4, T2, A6, and the tracking sheet in T5.\nDuring the pilot, I will also collect feedback from clerks on what works and what feels confusing so we can log it in A7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12",
            "T4",
            "T2",
            "A6",
            "T5",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            330756
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 330756,
          "reply_to": "M56",
          "text": "Thanks, that training will help.\nDuring the pilot I will make sure to log every form and query in A2 and follow the routing and escalation rules.\nIf I run into anything unclear, I will note it so it can go into A7 for the review.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            319449
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 408577,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "To prepare for the pilot, I will:\n- Finalise T5 so that it mirrors the steps in A4 and includes fields for owner and due date.\n- Set up views in A2 to track inputs, approvals, and discrepancies.\n- Create the initial A7 log structure so we can capture issues as they happen.\nOnce that is ready, we can do a quick dry run with a small set of test data before the real cycle.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A4",
            "A2",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            107378
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 107378,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "Sounds good.\nI will support with the dry run by entering sample data and checking that the checklist in A4 and the tracking in T5 and A2 line up.\nDuring the actual pilot, I will also keep an eye on any confidentiality issues and note them in A7 if they occur.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T5",
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            408577
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 421608,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "During the pilot cycle, I will focus on reconciliations and on checking that invoice related steps in T10 integrate smoothly with the payroll workflow.\nAny issues I find will be logged in A7 with suggestions for adjustments before full rollout.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A7",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            408577,
            107378
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 319449,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "After the pilot, I suggest we run a short retrospective using A7 as input: what worked, what did not, and what we want to change.\nWe can then update A3, A6, and T12 if needed before declaring the workflow final.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A7",
            "A3",
            "A6",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            330756,
            408577,
            107378
          ]

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "On A3, I see the main incident types listed, but I wonder if we should separate urgent health issues from things that can wait until the end of the day.             "A3",
            "T4"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            518039
          ]

          "msg_id": "M29",
          "speaker_id": 95695,
          "reply_to": "M28",
          "text": "I agree. Sometimes I am not sure who to call first. In the A3 draft, there is a step to inform the office, but I do not know when to call emergency services directly. Could we add a clear line in T4 that says when we call emergency services and when we call the office only",

            518039

          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M28",
          "text": "That makes sense. I will update T4 so A3 has two main paths. One for urgent health issues where we call emergency services first and then inform the office, and another for non urgent issues where we log it and inform the office within the same shift.           "msg_id": "M31",
          "speaker_id": 520047,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "For kitchen related incidents, like repeated complaints about undercooked food or food arriving at the wrong temperature, can we add a step in A3 to notify the kitchen contact directly as well That way we can adjust A1 or T5 quickly if needed.",

          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M31",
          "text": "Good point. I will add a branch in T4 so that nutrition or food safety issues trigger a note to the kitchen contact, in addition to the normal reporting path. A3 will show this clearly so aides know who to call for which type of problem.",

          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted a first version of the pilot client list and route plan for T7, which will feed into A5. It includes 20 clients with preferred delivery windows and a proposed daily route that fits within working hours, with some buffer for delays. I tried to align the timing with the packing steps in T5 and the checks in A4. Please review if the order and timing look realistic from both the visit and kitchen sides.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4",
            "T7",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            518039,
            95695,
            157604,
            520047
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "Looking at A5, the route seems balanced. I like that you grouped nearby clients together. One concern is the tight window between stops 4 and 5, where both clients prefer early delivery. We might need a bit more buffer there in case of traffic or a longer conversation.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            92532
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 95695,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "I checked A5 and I am a bit worried about the number of floors without elevators on the afternoon route. That might slow us down more than expected. Maybe we can move one of those clients to the morning when we have more energy and time.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            92532
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 520047,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "From the kitchen side, the current A5 timing works with T5 and A4 as long as we start packing by 9.00. If the first delivery window moves earlier, we might struggle to finish the hot meals in time. So if we adjust the route, please keep the first stop no earlier than 10.00.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            92532,
            518039
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 157604,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "I agree with keeping the first stop at 10.00 or later. That gives us enough time to follow A4 and T5 properly without rushing the temperature checks. If we need to shift clients around, I suggest we move some of the later ones rather than the first two.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            520047
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M40",
          "text": "Good points. I will adjust A5 so that one of the early window clients moves slightly later, and I will move one of the no elevator clients to the morning route. That should give us more buffer between stops 4 and 5 and reduce the afternoon strain. I will keep the first stop at 10.00 to match the kitchen timing.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            518039,
            95695,
            520047
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M44",
          "text": "With those changes, the route looks more realistic. I suggest we test this version of A5 in a dry run for T9, using A4 and the visit checklist A2 end to end. That will give us real timing data before we approve the schedule.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4",
            "A2",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            92532
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 95695,
          "reply_to": "M45",
          "text": "I can join the dry run for T9. It would help me practice using A2 and A4 together. I might need a bit of guidance on how much time to spend at each stop so we do not fall behind.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A4",
            "T9"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            518039,
            92532
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M45",
          "text": "Great, let us schedule the T9 dry run for the day after tomorrow. We can simulate at least 5 stops from A5, including one with stairs and one with a tight time window. We will record timing, note any delays, and see how A2 and A4 fit into the visit flow.",

            "A5",
            "A2",
            "A4",
            "T9"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            518039,
            95695

          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 520047,
          "reply_to": "M47",
          "text": "On the kitchen side, we can prepare test meals for the T9 dry run and follow T5 and A4 as if it were a real day. That will also let us check how long packing actually takes and whether the food temperature holds up until the last simulated stop.",

            "T9"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            157604
          ]

          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 157604,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "I will handle the kitchen part of T9 with you. We will log packing start and end times, plus temperature readings, and share them along with your route timing so we can see the full picture.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M47",
          "text": "Dry run completed. We simulated 5 stops from A5. Overall timing was close to plan, but we saw that the second stop took 10 minutes longer due to stairs and conversation. We also noticed that we sometimes rushed the A2 checklist to catch up. We should add a bit more buffer between stops 2 and 3 and slightly shorten the planned visit time at the easiest stop.",

          "mentions": [
            518039,
            95695

        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "I agree with those adjustments. The dry run showed that we need a bit more breathing room after the more demanding stops. If we update A5 with a few extra minutes between those visits, I think the schedule will be safe enough for the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T9"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            92532
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 520047,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "From the kitchen side, T9 went well. Following T5 and A4, the food stayed within safe temperature ranges even at the last simulated stop. The only pressure point was when we tried to pack too many meals at once. We will slightly stagger packing to match the updated A5 timing.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A5",
            "T5",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            157604
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "I have now updated A5 with extra buffer after the more demanding stops and a small reduction at the easiest one. With these changes and the dry run results, I think the daily route and schedule are ready for the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            518039,
            95695,
            520047,
            157604

          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 518039,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "I support using this updated A5 as our approved route and schedule for the 20 pilot clients. The dry run and adjustments give me enough confidence that we can stay within working hours and still do proper checks.",

            "A5",
            "T9"

          "decision_refs": [

          "mentions": [
            92532

          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 520047,
          "reply_to": "M52",
          "text": "Given the T9 results and the updated A5, I do not see any kitchen reason to change the plan further. As long as we follow T5 and A4, we should be fine. I suggest we keep this schedule for launch and only revisit it if we see repeated delays or food temperature issues.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4",
            "T5",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            92532,
            518039
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 92532,
          "reply_to": "M55",

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

          "msg_id": "M17",
          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Starting the pricing and margin thread for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles project_title.\nI have uploaded the first draft of the pricing and margin model in A2, linked to the bundle definitions in A1 and tracked under T3.\nKey assumptions:\n- Target margin range: 45 to 55 percent for Core Connect and Secure Connect, 40 to 50 percent for Managed Workplace Light, and 50 to 60 percent for Support Plus.\n- Standard discounts: up to 15 percent for mid-market, up to 20 percent for enterprise renewals, and up to 10 percent for digital-native SMBs, with additional approvals required beyond that.\n- Volume-based discounts kick in at contract values above a defined threshold.\nPlease review the tabs in A2, especially the segment-specific views, and share concerns before we lock guardrails and the initial price list.",

          "msg_id": "M18",
          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": "M17",
          "text": "I have gone through A2 and cross-checked the dates with A6.\nFrom a project view, we need to finalize the target margin ranges and discount rules in the next two days so that finance can sign off and we can feed the numbers into sales materials and T10.\nQuestions:\n- For enterprise renewals, is the 20 percent discount ceiling realistic given current practice, or will sales push for more?\n- For Support Plus, the margin range looks healthy, but are we comfortable that the cost assumptions reflect the enhanced SLA we are planning?\nOnce we settle these points, I can coordinate a quick review with the finance controller.",

          "speaker_id": 90589,

          "text": "Looking at A2, a couple of observations from a market angle:\n- Core Connect: the base price for digital-native SMBs might be slightly high compared to what we see from cloud-first competitors. We may need to rely heavily on the basic security inclusion to justify it.\n- Enterprise renewals: the 20 percent discount cap could be tight for large multi-year deals. Maybe we can keep the cap but define a clear exception path for strategic accounts.\nFor T10, I suggest we track margin by segment and bundle so we can see quickly if any combination is underperforming after launch.",

          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "I checked the cost inputs in A2 against our last financial report.\n- For Managed Workplace Light, the assumed license costs look slightly conservative, which is good for protecting margin.\n- For Support Plus, I am not fully sure the overtime and staffing costs for the enhanced SLA are fully captured. We might be underestimating the cost for the highest support tier.\nBefore we lock the 50 to 60 percent margin range for Support Plus, we should validate those cost lines with finance under T3.",

          "text": "I might be reading A2 incorrectly, but on the discount tab it looks like the margin for some enterprise deals goes below 30 percent when the maximum discount is applied.\nIs that expected, or did I misinterpret the formula? If that is correct, should we lower the maximum discount or adjust the list price?",

          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": "M21",
          "text": "Good catch. You are right that in a few edge cases the margin dips below 30 percent when stacking the maximum discount with certain cost assumptions.\nI see two options:\n1) Reduce the maximum discount for those bundles in enterprise deals.\n2) Keep the discount ceiling but adjust list prices slightly upward for those specific configurations.\nGiven market sensitivity, I lean toward tightening the discount rules for the most cost-intensive bundles rather than raising list prices too much.\nI will adjust the formulas in A2 so that the margin floor does not go below 35 percent even at the maximum discount.",

        {

          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "That adjustment sounds reasonable.\nTo make this concrete, can we agree on a target margin range per bundle that we will not cross, and then define discount rules that respect that floor?\nFor example:\n- Core Connect and Secure Connect: 45 to 55 percent\n- Managed Workplace Light: 40 to 50 percent\n- Support Plus: 50 to 60 percent, but only after we validate the cost base\nIf we align on these ranges, I can take them to finance for confirmation and then we can treat them as guardrails for T3 and T10.",

          "mentions": [

        {

          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M23",
          "text": "I am comfortable with those ranges.\nOn discounts, I suggest we keep the caps you proposed earlier but add a simple approval rule:\n- Up to 10 percent: standard for all segments\n- 10 to 15 percent: requires sales manager approval\n- 15 to 20 percent: only for enterprise renewals with finance approval\n- Above 20 percent: exception only, with executive approval\nThis should give sales some flexibility while protecting margins.",

          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M24",
          "text": "The approval ladder looks workable.\nWe should also make sure these rules are clearly reflected in the sales enablement content in A7 later, so that reps know when they need extra approvals.\nFor Support Plus, once we validate the cost base, I would keep the 50 to 60 percent range but maybe set a hard floor at 45 percent for any exception deals.",

          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": "M23",
          "text": "Summarizing what I hear so far:\n- Margin guardrails per bundle: Core Connect and Secure Connect at 45 to 55 percent, Managed Workplace Light at 40 to 50 percent, Support Plus at 50 to 60 percent with a hard floor at 45 percent for exceptions.\n- Discount rules: standard up to 10 percent, 10 to 15 percent with sales manager approval, 15 to 20 percent for enterprise renewals with finance approval, and anything above 20 percent as an executive exception.\nIf we agree on this structure, I will update A2 and mark these as our target ranges and rules for the first launch.",

          "text": "Given the alignment here, I propose we formally adopt the margin ranges and discount rules summarized by 6784 as our guardrails for this launch.\nI will share them with the finance controller for confirmation, but unless finance raises a major concern, we will treat these as the baseline for T3 and T10.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "With those guardrails in place, I think we can move to finalizing the actual price points per segment in A2.\nOnce finance confirms, we should be ready to lock the initial price list and start feeding it into sales materials and GTM planning.",

          "speaker_id": 6784,

          "msg_id": "M34",
          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Opening the supplier and systems readiness thread for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles project_title.\nI have updated the integrated project plan and RAID log in A6 and drafted a supplier impact summary in A5, covering T4 and T7.\nHighlights:\n- Two key network suppliers and one security partner are directly impacted by the new SLAs in A1.\n- ERP and billing changes are mostly configuration, but we need to confirm how we represent Support Plus and Managed Workplace Light.\nWe need to confirm which supplier contracts must be updated before launch and agree on clear ERP and billing readiness criteria for go or no-go.\nPlease review A5 and the relevant sections in A6 and share your view on what must be in place before launch versus what can follow later.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "I have gone through A5.\nFor the network suppliers, the new uptime and response SLAs for Secure Connect and Support Plus are stricter than some of the current contract terms.\nMy view:\n- Supplier A: contract must be updated before launch, as their current SLA would not support our promise.\n- Supplier B: current terms are close enough; we can manage with an operational workaround and update the contract post-launch.\nFor the security partner, the SLA alignment looks fine, but we should confirm any additional reporting requirements they might have.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "From a product and service view, I agree that Supplier A must be aligned before we go live, otherwise we risk not meeting the SLAs in A1.\nFor Supplier B, I am comfortable with a short-term workaround if operations confirms they can handle it.\nOn the security partner, we should check if any new reporting or audit requirements affect our cost assumptions in A2, but that should not block launch if the core SLA is already aligned.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A2",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            447542,
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 83919,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "Looking at A6, I see several supplier-related tasks under T4, but I am not entirely sure which ones are critical for launch.\nDo we need all contract amendments signed before we can start selling, or can we proceed with some in principle agreements while the paperwork is finalized?\nI want to make sure we do not delay the launch unnecessarily, but also that we are not exposed on the SLA side.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": "M37",
          "text": "Good question.\nMy proposal:\n- For Supplier A, we require a signed contract amendment before launch, as the gap to our promised SLA is material.\n- For Supplier B and the security partner, we can proceed with written confirmation of intent and operational workarounds, with formal contract updates scheduled within a defined period after launch.\nI will still ask legal to confirm this approach, but from a project risk view it seems balanced.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            83919,
            447542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "On ERP and billing under T7, I checked with the team informally.\n- Core Connect and Secure Connect can be represented with existing product codes plus minor configuration.\n- Managed Workplace Light will need a new bundle configuration, but no new product codes.\n- Support Plus requires a new billing rule for the premium support fee.\nI think our readiness criteria should include at least: correct bundle representation in the catalog, accurate billing rules for Support Plus, and the ability to report revenue by bundle for T10.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T7",
            "A6",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "I agree with those criteria.\nWe should also check that the ERP can handle the different discount rules we defined in A2, especially the approval steps, even if some of that is handled outside the system initially.\nFor the go or no-go, I would at least require that the system prevents discounts beyond the maximum without manual approval, or that we have a clear manual control in place.",
          "artifact_refs": [

            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            90589
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "From a reporting and KPI view, having revenue by bundle and segment available from day one will be important for T10 and A8 later.\nIf the ERP cannot provide that immediately, we should at least have a reliable interim report from billing or finance.\nI would include that as part of the readiness criteria, even if the first reports are manual.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A8",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 83919,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "So, to recap on suppliers, just to check my understanding:\n- Supplier A: contract amendment signed before launch.\n- Supplier B: written confirmation and workaround, contract update after launch.\n- Security partner: written confirmation, contract update later if needed.\nIf that is correct, I can help update A5 and A6, but I would appreciate someone reviewing my entries to ensure I do not miss any legal nuance.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217,
            447542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "You summarized it correctly.\nI will ask legal to review the plan, but from a project standpoint we can treat these three items as the supplier contract requirements for launch.\nI will mark Supplier A contract amendment as a pre-launch must-have in A6 and the others as post-launch follow-ups.",

            "A6",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [

          ],
          "mentions": [
            83919
          ]

        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M40",
          "text": "On the discount controls, the ERP team told me that enforcing approval steps directly in the system will take longer than our launch window.\nAs an interim solution, we can implement a manual approval process with a simple form and weekly audit, and then automate it later.\nI would still include a basic system check to prevent discounts above an absolute maximum, even if the detailed approval ladder is manual at first.",

            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M44",
          "text": "That compromise works for me.\nFor the readiness criteria, we can state that the system enforces a hard maximum discount and that a manual approval process is in place for anything above the standard levels.\nWe can then plan the full automation as a post-launch improvement in A6.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],

        {
          "msg_id": "M46",

          "text": "Starting the GTM and sales enablement thread for the Launch of Unified B2B Service Bundles project_title.\nI have uploaded a draft GTM playbook in A3 and initial sales one-pagers in A7, based on the bundle definitions in A1 and pricing in A2, tracked under T5 and T8.\nHighlights:\n- Positioning themes per bundle: reliability for Core Connect, protection for Secure Connect, productivity for Managed Workplace Light, and peace of mind for Support Plus.\n- Channel tactics: direct sales focus on enterprise renewals, inside sales and partners for mid-market and digital-native SMBs.\n- Draft internal communication outline linked to T11.\nPlease review A3 and A7 and share feedback on messaging, structure, and any gaps for sales conversations.",

          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "Good point.\nMy intent was for partners to lead with Core Connect and then position Managed Workplace Light as an upsell for customers who are already buying collaboration tools.\nI will make that explicit in A3 and add a simple decision tree for partners.\nOn the internal communication side under T11, I will also include a short guide for partner managers.",

          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "Agree on showing ranges and typical discounts rather than full price tables in A7.\nWe can include a note that detailed pricing is available in A2 and that any discount beyond the standard band requires approval, consistent with what we agreed in the pricing thread.\nI can help refine the FAQ for Support Plus to align with the SLA and scope in A1.",

          "speaker_id": 83919,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "On the internal communication plan under T11, do we plan a single company-wide announcement or separate messages for sales, support, and partners?\nI am asking because support might need more operational detail than sales, and partners might need a different angle.",

          "msg_id": "M75",
          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M72",
          "text": "On suppliers and financial aspects:\n- Supplier A contract amendment: signed and filed, as reflected in A5 and A4.\n- Supplier B and security partner: written confirmations received, with contract updates planned post-launch.\n- Budget and margin checks: aligned with finance based on A2.\nNo blocking issues from my side, but we should keep an eye on the operational performance of Supplier A in the first weeks.",

          "text": "On ERP and billing under T7:\n- Bundle configurations: Core Connect, Secure Connect, Managed Workplace Light, and Support Plus are configured and tested.\n- Billing rules: Support Plus premium fee is working in test, and the hard maximum discount is enforced.\n- Reporting: we have a manual report template for revenue by bundle and segment.\nIn A4, I flagged one open item: we still need final confirmation from the ERP team that there are no remaining critical defects. They said they will confirm by tomorrow.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M77",
          "speaker_id": 82217,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "Thanks for the updates.\nFrom the consolidated view in A4 and A6, I see:\n- All functional areas are green or amber, with no red items.\n- The main amber items are partner examples and final ERP confirmation, both expected to close within a day.\nGiven the fixed launch date, my inclination is to proceed as go, provided we get the ERP confirmation and partner examples in time.\nAny strong objections?",

          "speaker_id": 6784,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "No objections from my side.\nThe remaining items look manageable, and we have clear owners and timelines.\nI support proceeding as go, assuming the ERP team confirms no critical defects.",

            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            82217
          ]

          "speaker_id": 90589,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "I am also in favor of go.\nFor the partner examples, I can finalize a short addendum to A7 by tomorrow and share it with partner managers, so that should not hold us back.",

            "A4"

            82217

          "speaker_id": 447542,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "From a supplier and financial risk view, I am comfortable proceeding.\nWe should, however, make sure that any early issues with Supplier A or billing are captured quickly in the post-launch review framework in A8.",

            "A4"

          ]

          "speaker_id": 83919,
          "reply_to": "M77",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

          "speaker_id": 561948,
          "reply_to": "M1",
          "text": "Adding to what was shared:\n- Sometimes the first contact is only a phone call and we do not keep a record until the job is confirmed.\n- For some customers we send a quote first, but the quote is in a separate file and not linked to the final invoice.\n- For multi-day moves, I have seen partial notes for each day, which makes it harder to see the full job cost and revenue.\nI think for A1 we should include the quote step as well, even if we later decide the standard process officially starts at confirmation.\nOn the end point, I would lean towards ending the process when the invoice is posted in the ledger, and treat payment and reminders as part of a separate collection process.",

            "A1"

        {
          "msg_id": "M5",
          "speaker_id": 476700,
          "reply_to": "M1",
          "text": "I can help with T1 by pulling a few recent invoices and matching them to the job notes we received.\nOne thing I am not fully sure about is whether we should include the payment matching step in this same process map or keep it separate.\nAlso, for movers data, I often see only total hours and no breakdown of driving versus loading, and I do not know if we need that split for accounting or just for operations.\nMaybe we can clarify what is really mandatory for the books versus nice to have for planning.",

          "mentions": [

        {
          "msg_id": "M6",
          "speaker_id": 253807,
          "reply_to": "M5",
          "text": "Thanks all, this is very helpful.\nOn start and end points, here is a proposal for us to react to:\n- Start: when a move is confirmed with the customer (accepted quote or verbal confirmation) and we have at least customer name, address, date, and agreed service.\n- End: when the invoice is posted in the ledger with the correct VAT and supporting job documentation attached.\nPayment collection would then sit in a separate process.\nOn data from movers, from an accounting and tax perspective, I see the following as candidates for mandatory fields:\n- Customer name and address\n- Job date(s)\n- Description of service (e.g. local move, long-distance, packing included)\n- Hours worked and rate basis (hourly or fixed price)\n- Any extra billable items (packing materials, extra stops)\n- Confirmation that the job is completed\nLet us discuss if this list is realistic on the truck side before we lock it in for A1 and the later job sheet in A2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A2",
            "T1"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            395422,
            483272,
            561948,

        {

          "speaker_id": 395422,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "From the truck, your list mostly works, but I want to check a couple of points:\n- For description of service, would a few standard options help, like local move, long-distance, packing, storage? That would be faster than writing long text.\n- For hours, I can record start and end time and breaks. If you need the split between driving and loading, I can try, but it may slow us down.\n- Extra billable items: I can tick boxes for packing materials and extra stops, and maybe write a short note if something unusual happens.\nIf we keep it to ticks and short numbers, I can fill it in between tasks without holding up the team.",
          "artifact_refs": [],

          "mentions": [

          "msg_id": "M8",
          "speaker_id": 483272,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "On the accounting side, I do not need a detailed narrative for every job, but I do need enough to justify the invoice if we are audited.\nStandard options for service type would be fine as long as they map clearly to the correct revenue account and VAT code in A3 later.\nFor hours, total billable hours per job are essential. The split between driving and loading is more for operations, so I would not make that mandatory for accounting.\nI would add one more mandatory item: whether the customer is a business or a private person, because that can affect the invoice fields and sometimes the tax treatment.\nWe can reflect all of this in A1 and then design A2 around it.",
          "artifact_refs": [

            561948

        {
          "msg_id": "M9",
          "speaker_id": 561948,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "I agree with the proposal to start at confirmation and end at posting.\nFor mandatory data from movers, I would summarise it as:\n- Customer details (name, address, business or private)\n- Job date and location\n- Service type (from a short list)\n- Total billable hours or fixed price flag\n- Extra billable items (tick boxes plus short note if needed)\n- Job completion confirmation (for example, a simple yes or customer signature)\nThis feels manageable and should cover what we need for T1 and later for the job sheet in A2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T1",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            253807,
            395422

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M10",
          "speaker_id": 476700,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "I am fine with not including the payment matching step in this process.\nFor the movers data, I just want to check if we also need distance or route information for any tax reasons, or if that is only for pricing.\nIf it is only for pricing, maybe we can keep it optional and let operations decide how they want to track it.\nOnce we confirm the list, I can help check a few recent jobs to see if we already have most of this information or if we need to change how we collect it.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M11",
          "speaker_id": 253807,
          "reply_to": "M10",
          "text": "On distance and route: from a tax and bookkeeping point of view, we do not need exact kilometres for each job as long as the price and VAT are correct and we can explain the service.\nDistance is more relevant for pricing and planning, so I suggest we keep it optional for accounting and let operations decide if they want it for their own analysis.\nGiven the feedback so far, I propose we close two points:\n1) Process scope: start at job confirmation with minimum customer and job details; end at invoice posting in the ledger.\n2) Mandatory data from movers for accounting: customer details (including business or private), job date and address, service type from a list, total billable hours or fixed price flag, extra billable items, and job completion confirmation.\nIf anyone disagrees, please comment today; otherwise I will update A1 and T1 accordingly and treat this as agreed.",

          "text": "From my side, I would add a small section for notes on damage or special situations.\nRight now, movers sometimes send separate photos or messages, and it is hard to link them to the right job.\nIf we have a notes box on A2, we can refer to it when issuing the invoice or handling complaints.\nApart from that, I agree with the suggestions from the others.",

          "msg_id": "M29",
          "speaker_id": 253807,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted the chart of accounts and posting rules for moving services in A3, and the invoice and quote templates in A4, covering T3, T4, and part of T6.\nKey points in A3:\n- Separate revenue accounts for local moves, long-distance, packing, and storage, aligned with the LM, LD, PK, ST codes from A2.\n- Standard VAT code for domestic moves, with a note that cross-border or special cases must be checked with the tax advisor.\n- Posting rules for typical transactions: standard move, move with packing materials, and move with storage.\nIn A4, the invoice and quote templates include all mandatory legal fields, customer tax number for business customers, and a clear breakdown of services and VAT.\nPlease review and comment on:\n1) Whether the account structure is clear enough for daily posting.\n2) Any missing scenarios in the posting rules.\n3) Whether the invoice and quote templates are practical for our use and compliant with our obligations.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "T3",
            "T4",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [

        {
          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 483272,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "I have gone through A3 and A4.\nOn the chart of accounts, the separate revenue accounts per service type make sense and will help with reporting.\nFor posting rules, I would add an example for a job that includes both moving and storage, where storage is billed monthly.\nOn the invoice template in A4, I see all the usual legal fields, but I am not sure if we need a specific reference to the job sheet number from A2.\nIf we add a field for job sheet number, it will be easier to link invoices to the underlying documentation.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            253807
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M31",
          "speaker_id": 561948,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "I like the structure in A3.\nOne question: for packing materials, do we treat them as part of the moving service revenue or as separate goods revenue?\nFrom what I have seen, we usually include them in the service, but I want to be sure this is correct for tax and reporting.\nOn A4, the quote template mirrors the invoice nicely, which should reduce differences between what we promise and what we bill.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            253807,
            483272

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M32",
          "speaker_id": 476700,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "I have a small doubt about the VAT codes in A3.\nFor domestic moves, we use the standard VAT rate, but what about moves that start here and end in another country?\nI do not feel confident deciding that, so I think we should have a clear note that these cases must be checked with the tax advisor before invoicing.\nMaybe we can add a short section in A3 and T6 about special cases and who to contact.",

          "speaker_id": 253807,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "Good points.\nOn job sheet numbers, I agree we should add a field on A4 to reference the job sheet from A2. That will help with audit trails and error tracking in A6.\nOn packing materials, my proposal is:\n- Treat standard packing materials used as part of the move as service revenue under the same account and VAT code as the move.\n- Only use a separate goods revenue account if we sell materials separately without a move.\nThis keeps things simple and aligned with how we actually work.\nFor cross-border moves, I agree with the concern. I will add a clear note in A3 and T6 that any cross-border or unusual tax situations must be checked with the tax advisor before issuing the invoice.\nPlease confirm if you are comfortable with this approach so we can move towards approving the chart of accounts and templates for the pilot.",

          "speaker_id": 483272,
          "reply_to": "M33",
          "text": "I am fine with treating standard packing materials as part of the service revenue, and using a separate account only when we sell materials alone.\nAdding the job sheet reference on A4 and the special case note in A3 and T6 should cover the main risks.\nI would also suggest we include one worked example per service type in A3, showing the debit and credit entries, so that anyone posting can follow the pattern easily.",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

GLOSSARY (only for conceptual consistency; do NOT cite this in the output)

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)

* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

          "speaker_id": 313168,

          "text": "On T3 and A3, I have drafted a triage protocol with three urgency levels plus a fast-track for very simple visits.\nKey elements:\n- Level 1: emergency, immediate nurse and physician review.\n- Level 2: urgent, triage within 15 minutes.\n- Level 3: routine, triage within 60 minutes.\n- Fast-track: simple administrative or follow-up visits that can be handled quickly.\nEscalation criteria include chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe pain, and other red flags.\nPlease review A3 and let me know if the categories and response times are realistic for our clinic, and if there are any conditions we should add or clarify.",

          "text": "I have drafted:\n- a Daily Check-in and Triage Quality Control Checklist in A4 (for T4)\n- an incident and improvement log template in A6 (for T12), which we can also use during the pilot.\nThe checklist covers key steps at reception and triage, including data completeness, consent, and triage level documentation.\nThe log template has fields for date, time, description, category, impact, and follow-up.\nPlease review and share feedback on:\n1) Are we checking the right things daily, or is anything missing or unnecessary?\n2) How often should we run audits per shift, and who should be responsible?\n3) How should we categorise incidents and improvement suggestions in A6 so that we can review them efficiently?",

          "reply_to": "M40",
          "text": "Thanks for the feedback.\nI will update A4 to:\n- include a small sample check comparing paper forms and EHR entries\n- add items on visibility of allergies and medications at triage\n- provide brief guidance text for each checklist item.\nFor A6, I will add the categories suggested by 313168 and include a field for whether the entry is an incident or an improvement idea.\nNext, we should agree on D5: daily audit routine, responsibilities, and minimum compliance threshold.\nMy proposal:\n- One checklist per shift (morning, afternoon, evening), covering a sample of 5 patients.\n- A designated person per shift, rotating weekly.\n- Minimum compliance threshold: 90 percent of sampled records must meet all mandatory checks, with action required if we fall below this for more than two consecutive days.\nPlease share if this feels realistic or if we need to adjust the sample size or threshold.",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

        {
          "msg_id": "M27",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M26",
          "text": "Those three colors are fine, as long as we keep it to just those.\nWe can add a small legend in A8 and in the training checklist A6 so new staff can learn it quickly.\nFor T2, please also add a field on the label for zone code, so we can see at a glance where the order should be.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M28",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M20",
          "text": "On the zoning approach, I propose we standardise it as:\n- S shelves for small orders (S1, S2, S3)\n- B floor zones for bulky orders (B1, B2)\n- F rack for floral and garden orders\nThis way, when we plan routes in T9, movers know exactly where to drop items, and sales know where to look.",

            27468

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M29",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "For perishable bakery items, I will add into A3 that we avoid placing them near heaters or in direct sunlight, and that we prioritise earlier pickup windows.\nOn the labels, having the pickup deadline time will also help us decide when to start calling customers, which we can later reflect in A5 for reminder messages.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M28",
          "text": "Let me try to summarise the proposed standard so we can confirm it.\nLabel format for T2:\n- Fields: order ID, customer name, phone, short item description, pickup deadline date and time, zone code\n- Color dots: red for fragile, blue for bulky, green for perishable, based on A3\nStorage zoning:\n- S1, S2, S3 shelves for small orders\n- B1, B2 floor zones for bulky orders near the back, with clear paths\n- F rack for floral and garden orders, aligned with A4 and T6\nHandling rules from A3 and A4:\n- Fragile: no stacking, single layer\n- Bulky: stacking allowed only when packaging supports it\n- Perishable: no heavy items on top, away from heat and direct sun\n- Floral: light but not harsh sun, watering rules defined in T6\nIf everyone is ok with this, we can lock it in and I will help document it in A3, A4, and A8.",
