          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have a first draft of the order tracking sheet for T5 in A2, plus a simple proposal for filing rules for T12.\nTracking sheet A2 fields:\n- Order ID\n- Customer name\n- Phone\n- Items summary\n- Status (codes below)\n- Pickup deadline date and time\n- Zone code (S1, B1, F, etc.)\n- Notes\nStatus codes proposal:\n- NEW: order taken, not yet picked\n- PICKING: items being collected\n- STAGED: ready in staging area\n- READY: confirmed and ready for pickup\n- PICKED: customer collected\n- CANCELLED\nFor T12, I suggest we keep paper receipts in daily folders and scan them weekly into a digital folder structure by month and then by order ID.\nPlease review and tell me what is missing or unclear.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            27468,
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "The structure in A2 looks solid.\nTwo suggestions:\n1) Add a field for payment method, so we can quickly see if a refund should go back to card or cash when we work on T8.\n2) For status codes, maybe we can merge READY and STAGED into one, or clearly define the difference. Otherwise staff may not use them consistently.\nOn T12, we should also define a retention period for the digital files, in line with our existing rules.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T8",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "From the sales counter, the status codes NEW and PICKING are clear.\nI am not sure when we should move from STAGED to READY. Is READY only after office has checked the order and label, or as soon as we place it in the zone?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "For movers, it would help if A2 shows at what time we are expected to move bulky items.\nMaybe we can use the Notes field to add a time slot, or add a simple 'Mover slot' column.\nAlso, for T12, if we scan delivery notes, we should make sure the scanned file name includes the order ID so we can find it quickly.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M36",
          "text": "Good points.\nOn status codes, I propose we keep both STAGED and READY but define them clearly in A7:\n- STAGED: items are in the staging area but not yet checked against the checklist A8\n- READY: items checked, label confirmed, and customer can be called\nThis way we can use READY as the trigger for customer communication in A5.\nFor T12, I will check with our existing retention rules, but I expect we will need to keep digital files for several years.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A7",
            "A8",
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "I like that distinction.\nWe can also add a short description of each status directly in A2, so staff do not need to open A7 every time.\nOn T12, I suggest we define:\n- Paper: kept for one year in store\n- Digital: kept for the legal retention period in the central drive\nWe will still need management to confirm the exact number of years, but we can document the structure now.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "With that definition, at the counter we will know that once we finish picking and movers have dropped bulky items, we set the status to STAGED.\nThen office can move it to READY after checking A8.\nThat seems clear enough for us.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "On the mover slot, maybe we can avoid another column and just use a simple code in Notes like 'Mover 10:00' or 'Mover 15:00'.\nThat should be enough for planning T9 without making A2 too wide.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Agreed. I will keep the Notes field and use it for mover time slots.\nFor T12, I will define the digital naming convention as 'OrderID_CustomerName_Date', so we can search by any of those.\nWe will also test retrieval of three sample orders as required by T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "One more detail: for T5 we should test A2 with at least five mock orders, including one cancellation and one late pickup.\nThat will help us see if the status codes and fields cover the main cases, especially when we link them to the issue guide A7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M35",
          "text": "For us at the counter, the key is that we can quickly see if an order is READY or not.\nAs long as A2 is easy to filter by status and customer name, we will be able to answer customers without calling the office every time.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M44",
          "text": "I will set up simple filters in A2 so we can sort by status and search by name or phone.\nLet me summarise the final structure and rules so we can confirm them:\nFields in A2 for T5:\n- Order ID\n- Customer name\n- Phone\n- Items summary\n- Payment method\n- Status (NEW, PICKING, STAGED, READY, PICKED, CANCELLED)\n- Pickup deadline date and time\n- Zone code\n- Notes (including mover time slots)\nStatus definitions will be documented in A2 and A7.\nArchiving rules for T12:\n- Paper: daily folders in store, kept for one year\n- Digital: scanned weekly, stored by month and order ID, with file names 'OrderID_CustomerName_Date', kept for the legal retention period in the central drive (exact years to be confirmed by management).\nIf this works for everyone, we can treat it as our standard.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "T5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            27468,
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "This summary covers what we need.\nI am ok to approve these fields and codes for A2 and the archiving approach for T12, pending the final retention period confirmation from management.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "Works for movers as well. The Notes field and zone code will be enough for planning our daily runs.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M49",

          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I drafted initial customer communication templates for T4 and a basic procedure for cancellations and partial pickups for T8.\nIn A5 we have three main templates:\n1) Order confirmation: thanks the customer, lists items summary, pickup location, and standard pickup window (for example, within 3 days), plus what documents to bring.\n2) Ready for pickup: confirms that the order status in A2 is READY, repeats pickup location and deadline.\n3) Delay notice: explains that one or more items are delayed, gives a new expected date, and offers options (wait, partial pickup, or cancellation).\nFor T8, the draft procedure is:\n- Partial pickup: office updates A2 to show which items were picked, keeps the order open for the remaining items, and notes it on the paper receipt.\n- Cancellation: office sets status to CANCELLED in A2, processes refund in POS according to existing rules, and files documents per T12.\nPlease review the wording and the steps, especially from the sales and mover side, to see if anything is missing for real conversations with customers.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A2",
            "T4",
            "T8",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            27468,
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "The structure in A5 looks good.\nI would add a short line in the confirmation and ready messages about how long we will keep the order before we cancel it, to set expectations.\nOn T8, for cancellations we should also mention in the template that refunds follow our standard store policy, so staff do not promise anything outside existing POS rules.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "At the counter, customers often ask if someone else can pick up for them.\nShould we add in A5 what they need to bring if a friend or family member comes instead, like the order confirmation and an ID?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "From the moving side, the main impact is when there is a delay or partial pickup for bulky items.\nIt would help if the delay notice in A5 includes a short explanation that large items may need extra time to be moved to the staging area, so customers understand why they might wait a bit longer.\nFor T8, when a partial pickup involves a bulky item, we should note clearly in A2 which part was taken, so we do not move the same item twice.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A2",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M52",
          "text": "Good point.\nI will add a line in the confirmation and ready templates in A5 explaining that a third person can pick up the order if they bring the order confirmation and an ID that matches the name on the order, or a simple authorisation note if our policy allows it.\nWe will need management to confirm the exact rule, but we can prepare the wording now.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "On partial pickups for T8, I suggest we standardise how we write it in A2 and on the paper receipt.\nExample: in A2 Notes we write 'Customer picked 2 of 4 items on date, remaining 2 pending', and on the receipt we circle the items taken.\nThis will make it easier to resolve issues later and to document them in A7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "That helps.\nAt the counter we can follow that pattern when someone only takes part of the order, and then call the office to update A2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "For bulky items, maybe the delay notice in A5 can say something like 'Large items may require extra preparation time in the store'.\nThat keeps it honest without going into too much detail.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "Let me summarise the key points to include in A5 and T8 based on the feedback:\n- All templates will clearly state the pickup window and how long we keep the order before cancellation.\n- Confirmation and ready messages will explain what documents are needed, including rules for third-party pickup (to be validated by management).\n- Delay notice will mention that large items may need extra preparation time.\n- For cancellations, templates will say that refunds follow our standard store policy.\n- For partial pickups, we will document in A2 Notes which items were taken and mark them on the paper receipt.\nDoes this cover the main needs from sales and movers?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A2",
            "T4",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            27468,
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "From my side this is complete.\nOnce management signs off on the templates in A5, we can treat them as the standard for launch.\nFor T8, we should also add a short escalation note in A7 for complex cases, like repeated delays or disputes about refunds.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "This works for the counter.\nHaving clear wording in A5 will make it easier to answer questions without improvising.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "No further comments from movers. The mention of extra preparation time for large items is enough for us.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M62",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M59",
          "text": "Given the feedback, I propose we:\n- Approve the structure of the three main templates in A5 for launch, subject to final wording approval by store management.\n- Confirm the process in T8 for handling partial pickups, cancellations, and delays, including how we update A2 and file documents under T12.\nI will send A5 and the T8 procedure to management for formal approval, but for our work here we can treat them as final.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A2",
            "T4",
            "T8",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",

          ],

            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M63",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M62",
          "text": "Agreed. From an office perspective, we can go ahead with these as our standard, pending management sign-off.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [

        {
          "msg_id": "M64",
          "speaker_id": 27468,

          "artifact_refs": [

        {
          "msg_id": "M66",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I drafted a first version of the training checklist for T7 in A6 and wanted to propose a go-live date.\nTraining checklist A6 sections:\n- Sales floor: how to look up orders in A2, how to read labels from T2, when to call office, basic answers for customers.\n- Office: how to update statuses in A2, use templates in A5, handle T8 cases.\n- Movers: how to follow A3 and A8, where to drop bulky items, and how to plan daily runs from T9.\n- Specialised sellers: key points from A4 and T6.\nI was thinking we could aim for go-live in about two weeks, if we can finish the trainings by then.\nDoes this timing sound realistic, and what should we add to the checklist?",

          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted an initial proposal for the maintenance and inspection schedule for T6, which will feed into the Maintenance and Inspection Master Schedule A5.\n\nProposal by building category:\n- Newer buildings (under 15 years): annual full inspection, quarterly common-area checks, and statutory safety checks as required.\n- Older buildings (15 years and above): full inspection every 6 months, quarterly common-area checks, and more frequent checks on known risk areas.\n- Small blocks: annual inspection plus visits triggered by tenant reports.\n\nThis is based on the current inventory and condition data we have in A4 and my experience with building codes. Please review and suggest adjustments, especially around combining these with the compliance checklist from T12 so we minimise tenant disruption.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T6",
            "A4",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424,
            52814,
            128593,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "From what I see on site, the proposed frequencies are reasonable, especially the more frequent checks for older buildings.\n\nTo make this workable, we should:\n- Group inspections by area so we can cover several nearby buildings in one round.\n- Combine general condition checks with the safety and energy items from T12 where possible.\n\nI can help refine A5 once we have the full inventory from T5 updated in A4.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12",
            "T5",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "From a tenant and owner communication angle, it is important that the inspection frequencies in A5 match what we say in the rental agreements A3 and the notices from T9.\n\nIf we go with 6-monthly inspections for older buildings, we should make that clear in the contract and FAQ so tenants are not surprised by visits.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A3",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "I can help by setting up A5 as a shared sheet with filters by building type, age, and location. That should make it easier for 167424 and other caretakers to plan routes.\n\nJust to confirm: for the compliance checklist in T12, do we want all items to be mandatory for every building, or will there be exceptions by building type?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M45",
          "text": "For T12, my view is that the core health, safety and energy items should be mandatory for all buildings, regardless of age. Some additional checks might be specific to certain systems, but the baseline should be the same.\n\nWe can mark optional items in T12, but the main checklist should apply portfolio-wide.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "Agree on having one baseline checklist in T12. It makes training easier. We can add a short note for items that only apply if the building has certain systems, like lifts or underground parking.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "On grouping by area, once T5 is complete and A4 is up to date, we can cluster buildings by postcode and building type in A5. That will help us plan inspection routes and reduce travel time.\n\nWe should also flag in A5 any buildings with known high-risk issues so they get priority slots.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A4",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "Looking at this from a risk perspective, I want to be sure that our inspection frequencies in A5 are clearly in line with safety and energy regulations.\n\nCan we double-check the proposed intervals against regulatory guidance, especially for fire safety and gas installations, before we finalise A5? If needed, we can ask the legal and compliance team to confirm.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M49",
          "text": "Yes, I will cross-check the proposed frequencies with current regulations and manufacturer recommendations. For any grey areas, I will ask legal and compliance to validate before we lock A5.\n\nIn practice, our proposal is already slightly more frequent than the minimum in most cases, which should give us a safety margin.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "Once A4 is fully updated from T5, I can propose a first pass of grouped inspection routes in A5 for the two main city clusters. That will show if the schedule is realistic in terms of workload.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A5",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M45",
          "text": "I have created the initial structure for A5 with columns for building ID, type, age band, location, inspection type, frequency, and next due date. Once T5 and T12 are final, we can populate and standardise the entries.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "I have now incorporated feedback and regulatory checks into the proposal for A5:\n- Newer buildings: annual full inspection plus statutory checks.\n- Older buildings: full inspection every 6 months plus statutory checks.\n- Small blocks: annual inspection plus triggered visits.\n\nAll of these include the mandatory items from T12. I propose we adopt this as our standard inspection frequency and scope for each building category.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            167424,
            52814,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "From my side, these frequencies are acceptable and can be reflected in the tenant communication and contract wording. As long as we keep tenants informed via the notices from T9, this should not create undue friction.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "The updated schedule in A5 looks workable. The 6-monthly checks for older buildings will help us catch issues earlier. I support using this as the standard going forward.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "Given the confirmations and the regulatory check you mentioned, I am comfortable approving these inspection frequencies and scopes in A5 as our standard for the first wave.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "On T12, I have reviewed the checklist items and aligned them with regulatory requirements: fire safety, access, ventilation, and energy performance are all included as mandatory items.\n\nI propose we confirm T12 as the standard compliance checklist for all buildings, with only a few conditional items marked as 'if applicable'.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            167424,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "I have tested T12 on one of the older buildings. It covers the key safety and energy points without being too long. I support using it as the standard checklist for all buildings.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "With your test and the regulatory alignment, we will confirm T12 as the mandatory compliance checklist across the portfolio. Any future regulatory changes can be handled as updates to this single list.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424
          ]
        }

          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have created a first version of the property performance dashboard template for T7, which is now set up as A6.\n\nCurrent KPIs:\n- Occupancy rate by building and overall.\n- Rent arrears (amount and percentage).\n- Number of open maintenance issues and average age.\n- Inspection status from A5 (on track, overdue).\n- Number of complaints and average resolution time.\n\nPlease review and suggest any additional metrics or simplifications. We also need to agree how often we share this with owners and senior management, and who updates which fields, as per T7 and T8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T7",
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            54175,
            128593,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "The initial set of KPIs in A6 covers the essentials. I would add:\n- Turnaround time between move-out and next move-in, to track how quickly we re-let units.\n- Percentage of inspections completed on time, linked to A5.\n\nWe should also keep the number of metrics manageable so on-site staff are not overwhelmed with data entry.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M62",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "From a leasing and owner perspective, occupancy, arrears, and turnaround time are key. I would also consider:\n- Average achieved rent versus target, to see if we are pricing correctly.\n\nWe should avoid too many detailed financial metrics in A6, though, and leave deeper analysis to finance.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M63",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "For on-site staff, it would help if A6 clearly shows which data we need to update and how often. For example, inspections and open issues could be updated weekly, while some financial data might be monthly.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M64",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "For senior management, I would like A6 to give a quick view of:\n- Occupancy.\n- Arrears.\n- Major issues or risks.\n\nWe can keep the dashboard simple and use it in a monthly review. For owners, a quarterly summary might be enough, unless there are specific issues.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M65",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M61",
          "text": "I will add turnaround time and on-time inspection percentage to A6, and mark them as core KPIs.\n\nFor data entry, I will highlight which fields are updated by housing management, on-site staff, and finance, in line with T7.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M66",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M64",
          "text": "On cadence, I suggest:\n- Internal team: weekly review of A6 to catch issues early.\n- Senior management: monthly summary based on A6.\n- Owners: quarterly report, with ad-hoc updates if there are major incidents.\n\nThis should balance transparency with workload.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M67",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M66",
          "text": "I support that cadence. For owners, the quarterly report can highlight occupancy, arrears, and any significant maintenance or compliance actions, without going into too much operational detail.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M68",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M63",
          "text": "If we go with a weekly internal review, I can commit to updating inspection status and open issues in A6 once a week for my buildings. It would help if the dashboard clearly flags overdue items so we can prioritise.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M69",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M68",
          "text": "I will add simple colour coding in A6 for overdue inspections and long-open issues, so they stand out in the weekly review.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M70",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M60",
          "text": "Looking at the updated A6, I think the final set of KPIs should be:\n- Occupancy rate.\n- Rent arrears.\n- Turnaround time between tenancies.\n- Open maintenance issues and average age.\n- Inspection completion rate.\n- Complaints volume and resolution time.\n\nAdditional metrics like achieved rent versus target can be optional for now. This keeps the dashboard focused and actionable.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M71",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M70",
          "text": "I am comfortable with that list as the core KPIs in A6. We can always add more detail later if needed, but this covers the main drivers of performance.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M72",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M70",
          "text": "Agreed. Let us lock these as the standard KPIs for A6. They give a clear picture without being overwhelming.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M73",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M66",
          "text": "On reporting cadence, I support the proposal:\n- Weekly internal review using A6.\n- Monthly summary for senior management.\n- Quarterly report for owners, with ad-hoc updates for major issues.\n\nWe can formalise this in the communication plan under T8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M74",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M73",
          "text": "That cadence works for operations. We will build the weekly review into our routine and use it to catch issues before they show up in the monthly and quarterly reports.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M75",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M73",
          "text": "I will update T7 and T8 to reflect the agreed KPIs and reporting cadence, and I will document who updates which parts of A6 and when.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D7",
            "D8"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            48703
          ]
        }

          "msg_id": "M76",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "For the pilot of the centralised model under T10, I propose we use two buildings:\n- Building Alpha: newer, high-occupancy block in the first city cluster.\n- Building Beta: older walk-up with more frequent tenant changeovers in the second cluster.\n\nBoth are fully residential and already well documented in the inventory A4. They give us a good mix of stability and complexity.\n\nI have also drafted a simple communication outline for owners and tenants, based on A7, to explain what the pilot means for them. Please review the building choices and the communication approach before we confirm the pilot start date.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A4",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            52814,
            128593,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M77",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "From an on-site perspective, Alpha and Beta are good choices. I know both buildings well and can support the pilot activities there.\n\nWe should make sure the maintenance and inspection schedule from A5 is fully set up for these two before we start, so we do not confuse tenants with changing dates mid-pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M78",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "From the leasing side, Alpha and Beta will give us a good test of the new A2 checklist and A3 contract pack. Alpha has more stable tenants, while Beta will likely see more move-ins and move-outs during the pilot.\n\nFor owners, we should clearly explain in the A7 communication pack what changes for them in terms of reporting and decision-making, and what stays the same.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A3",
            "A7",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M79",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "I can help refine the owner and tenant messages in A7 and align them with the FAQ and notices from T9.\n\nDo we have a target start date in mind for the pilot in Alpha and Beta, or should we first confirm that all required documents and checklists (A2, A3, A5, A8) are ready?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A7",
            "T9",
            "A2",
            "A3",
            "A5",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M80",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M76",
          "text": "Alpha and Beta sound like sensible pilot choices. Before we confirm, I want to be sure that:\n- Owners of both buildings are comfortable with the pilot and the centralised model.\n- We have a clear incident and escalation procedure in place via A8 and T11.\n\nOnce those are in place, I would like us to set a firm pilot start date within the next two weeks.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8",
            "T11",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M81",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M80",
          "text": "On T11, I have drafted an incident and escalation procedure that will become A8. It defines incident categories, severity levels, and response time targets, and sets out who is contacted at each step.\n\nI will share it with 48703 and 167424 for practical feedback before we finalise it for the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M82",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M81",
          "text": "I have reviewed the draft A8. The categories and response times look reasonable. It would help if we include a simple step-by-step guide for on-site staff, so in an urgent situation they do not have to read a long document.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M83",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M81",
          "text": "I agree. A8 covers the right escalation paths. For the pilot, we should also make sure contact details are up to date and that there is a clear backup if someone is unavailable.\n\nOnce we add a short quick-reference section, I am comfortable using A8 in Alpha and Beta.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],

          "msg_id": "M19",
          "speaker_id": 246501,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Picking up on the themes from A1, let us start drafting customer guidance prompts for the top categories for T2.\nKey areas based on D1 are: finding products and related items, refunds and exchanges, and stock visibility.\nPlease share example opening questions you already use with customers and any phrases that work well when recommending products.\nWe will collect these into A2 and also feed into T5 for the refunds and exchanges quick guide.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A2",
            "T2",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M20",
          "speaker_id": 177366,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "For kids clothing, I usually ask:\n- What size is your child wearing now and how quickly are they growing?\n- Is this for everyday use or a special occasion?\nFor recommendations, I say things like:\n- This range has adjustable waistbands which help if you are between sizes.\n- Many parents choose this fabric because it is easier to wash and dry.\nNot sure if these need to be written in a more formal way for A2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M21",
          "speaker_id": 427273,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "For cleaning products and refills, I tend to ask:\n- What type of surface or material are you using this on?\n- Do you prefer fragrance-free or scented products?\n- How often do you plan to use it?\nThen I recommend by saying:\n- This option is more concentrated, so it lasts longer if you follow the dosing on the label.\n- Customers who buy this cleaner often take this refill as well so they do not run out.\nWe can standardise these in A2 under the cleaning category for T2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M22",
          "speaker_id": 486724,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "At the counter for refunds and exchanges, I usually start with:\n- Can you tell me what went wrong with the item so we can see the best option for you?\n- Do you prefer a refund, an exchange, or a voucher if that is available?\nFor T5, we should also include phrases like:\n- Let me quickly check our policy so we can do this correctly for you.\n- I will explain each step so you know what to expect.\nI can help structure these into a simple flow for A5 once we agree on the wording.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M23",
          "speaker_id": 244639,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "For stock visibility questions, I often say:\n- Let me check if we have more in the back or if another size is available.\nIf we do not have it, I say:\n- We are currently out of this size here, but I can check if another store has it or if we can order it.\nI am not sure how to turn this into prompts for A2, maybe someone can help phrase them better.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M24",
          "speaker_id": 246501,
          "reply_to": "M23",
          "text": "These are good starting points.\nI will draft a first version of A2 for T2 with 3 to 5 opening questions and 2 to 3 recommendation examples for:\n- Kids clothing\n- Cleaning products and refills\n- Promo items in the entrance aisle\n- High-questions products from T8 once we list them\n- Refunds and exchanges at the counter (linked to A5)\nOnce drafted, we will need to check them against company policy and get sign-off from the store manager or delegate.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2",
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            177366,
            427273,
            486724,
            244639
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M25",
          "speaker_id": 427273,
          "reply_to": "M24",
          "text": "When we write the prompts into A2, I suggest we keep them as short bullet points and avoid anything that sounds too scripted.\nFor example, instead of a long sentence, we can write:\n- Ask about who the item is for and how often they will use it.\n- Offer one main option and one alternative at a different price point.\nThis should make it easier for everyone to adapt the wording naturally while still covering the key points.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M26",
          "speaker_id": 177366,
          "reply_to": "M25",
          "text": "I like the idea of short bullet points. If the prompts are too long, I might forget parts of them when it is busy.\nMaybe we can also add one or two example phrases per category in A2 so newer staff have something concrete to start from.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            427273
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M27",
          "speaker_id": 486724,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "For T5, we should make sure the quick guide in A5 clearly follows company policies.\nI can draft the steps in order:\n1) Greet and listen to the issue\n2) Check receipt or proof of purchase\n3) Check item condition\n4) Confirm what options are allowed under policy\n5) Process refund or exchange and explain any notes on the receipt\nThen we can add the example phrases we discussed and send it to the customer service supervisor for review.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            246501
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M28",
          "speaker_id": 244639,
          "reply_to": "M25",
          "text": "I just want to check: will we be expected to say the prompts exactly as written, or can we change the wording as long as we cover the same points?\nI find it easier to speak in my own words, but I do not want to go against what is agreed.",

          "reply_to": "M28",
          "text": "Good question. My view is that prompts should guide the conversation, not be read word for word.\nWe can agree that everyone should cover the key questions and recommendations listed in A2, but they can adapt the exact phrasing to their style, as long as they stay within policy.\nWe should still check with the store manager when we share A2 to confirm they are comfortable with this approach.",

          "artifact_refs": [

        {

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M33",
          "speaker_id": 427273,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "I agree this can be our first version for the top categories.\nOn how strictly to follow them, I suggest we agree that:\n- Everyone should use the prompts as a checklist of points to cover\n- Staff can adapt the wording to suit the customer and situation\n- If someone wants to change the structure, they should share it in the channel so we can keep A2 updated\nIf we are aligned, we can record both the approval of the first version and this flexible use under D3 and D4.",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.

          "speaker_id": 36422,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "Looking at A6 and A7, the biggest gains came from the press and the sealer. The conveyor and case erector showed some improvement, but less pronounced. HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.

* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.

* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

DETERMINISTIC PROCEDURE (for each participant)
1. Collect candidate evidence:
   * Messages where speaker_id == the participant’s _id.
   * If the participant speaks little, you can also use messages that mention them (mentions contains _id) as contextual evidence.
2. For each attribute (productivity, ability, performance), mark:
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of HIGH => candidate HIGH
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of LOW  => candidate LOW
   * otherwise => MID
3. Attention:
   * If there are strong signals of HIGH and LOW at the same time for the same attribute, choose MID (conservative rule).
   * In the corporate context, everyone needs to deliver and demonstrate work; be careful to infer HIGH for something standard that should be MID.
   * Having one to four pieces of evidence for threads (<= 4 evidence items * threads) is not strong evidence.
4. Little evidence:
   * If there are no messages from the participant, use MID for all three attributes and use evidence from a message where they were mentioned.

EVIDENCE RULES (MANDATORY)
* For each participant, return 2 to 5 items in evidence.
* Each evidence item:
  * attribute ∈ {"productivity","ability","performance"}
  * msg_id must exist in the channel
  * justification: one sentence justifying the label.
  * snippet must be a short quote (up to ~20 words) copied from the text of that msg (no comment).
* Do not invent msg_id.
* Do not include “LOW/MID/HIGH” in the snippet.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.

          "speaker_id": 22473,

          "text": "We now have the first full cycle of pilot data and feedback. I pulled a summary from the KPI dashboard spec in A8 and the tracking work in T10 and T12.           "speaker_id": 94563,
          "reply_to": "M66",
          "text": "Looking at these numbers against the success metrics in A1, the pilot is performing well: conversion and early retention are both strong, and engagement metrics are healthy. The main friction points seem to be around exports and data freshness expectations. My initial recommendation would be to expand cautiously: open the subscription to a broader slice of the same segment while planning a short iteration to address the top issues in T12. I do not see a reason to pause given the current data.",

            "A1",

            "A8"

          "mentions": [

          "speaker_id": 132848,
          "reply_to": "M66",
          "text": "From the financial model in A2 and the early revenue numbers, the pilot is tracking slightly above the mid-case scenario we modelled in T4. If we expand to more mid-market accounts with similar conversion, we should hit the targets we set for the first year.           "speaker_id": 242297,
          "reply_to": "M66",
          "text": "Operationally, the onboarding process in A4 and T6 held up well.           "reply_to": "M66",

          "text": "I have posted the initial data architecture and API spec in A4, aligned with the MVP scope in A1 and the decisions from D1 and D2.\nFor T4, the proposal is:\n- Edge device collects sensor data and alarm states\n- Local buffering in a small queue on the device\n- MQTT to our backend with a simple JSON payload\n- Optional CSV export for the pilot plants\n\nFor T5, the first edge software iteration will focus on acquisition, buffering, and basic alarm evaluation only.\nI would like feedback on:\n- Any additional data fields needed for T7 tests or pilot analysis\n- Latency and reliability expectations from the application side\n- Any constraints from production on hardware resources that might affect the edge stack",

          "reply_to": "M32",
          "text": "Thanks for sharing A4.\nFrom an application and testing perspective for T7:\n- The data fields you listed cover what we need for the pilot acceptance criteria and for basic downtime analysis.\n- For latency, if we can keep end-to-end delay under a few seconds for alarms, that is enough for the first pilot.\n- Reliability: I would like the edge buffer to handle at least a few hours of data in case of network issues, so we do not lose events during short outages.\nIf we can meet these, I do not see a need to add more complexity in the first iteration.",

          "mentions": [

          "speaker_id": 29405,
          "reply_to": "M32",
          "text": "On hardware resource constraints from a build standpoint:\nWe have not finalized the exact controller yet, but for T6 and T8 I am assuming a modest embedded platform, not a high-end PC.\nIf the edge software in T5 can run with limited CPU and memory and does not require special storage beyond a small flash, that will help keep the BOM in A3 under control.\nIf you foresee any need for larger storage or more powerful hardware, please flag it early so we can factor it into T8.",

          "speaker_id": 219209,
          "reply_to": "M32",
          "text": "From the electrical side, the main concern is that the data architecture in A4 stays compatible with the I/O and power scheme in T3.\nAs long as the edge device can operate reliably on 24 VDC and does not require additional field wiring beyond what we already planned, I do not see major constraints.\nOne request: please make sure the edge software exposes clear status indicators (even if only via the backend or CSV) so we can correlate any electrical issues with data gaps during T7.",

          "speaker_id": 59849,
          "reply_to": "M33",
          "text": "On latency and buffering:\n- For alarms, I will target sub-second processing on the edge and a few seconds end-to-end to the backend, assuming normal network conditions.\n- For buffering, I will design T5 to store several hours of data in a local queue, with backoff and retry logic for MQTT.\nI will document these targets explicitly in A4 so they are visible in the test plan for T7.",

          "text": "On resource usage:\nThe current T5 plan is to use a lightweight runtime with:\n- Modest CPU needs (simple polling and threshold checks)\n- A small in-memory buffer plus periodic flush to flash\n- No heavy analytics or databases in the MVP\nThis should fit on a low to mid-range embedded controller. Always evaluate participants in relation to the group, that is, within the group itself, who stands out the most, who stands out the least, and who is average, using the criteria of HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

DETERMINISTIC PROCEDURE (for each participant)
1. Collect candidate evidence:
   * Messages where speaker_id == the participant’s _id.
   * If the participant speaks little, you can also use messages that mention them (mentions contains _id) as contextual evidence.
2. For each attribute (productivity, ability, performance), mark:

   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of LOW  => candidate LOW
   * otherwise => MID
3. Attention:
   * If there are strong signals of HIGH and LOW at the same time for the same attribute, choose MID (conservative rule).
   * In the corporate context, everyone needs to deliver and demonstrate work; be careful to infer HIGH for something standard that should be MID.
   * Having one to four pieces of evidence for threads (<= 4 evidence items * threads) is not strong evidence.
4. Little evidence:
   * If there are no messages from the participant, use MID for all three attributes and use evidence from a message where they were mentioned.

* Do not include “LOW/MID/HIGH” in the snippet.

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.

        {
          "msg_id": "M12",
          "speaker_id": 497314,
          "reply_to": "M5",
          "text": "On success criteria from a communication angle, I propose we also track whether students and hotel staff can accurately describe the programme goals after the initial briefing.\n\nWe can include a couple of simple questions in the pre and post tools that 36727 and 45096 will design for A5, to see if our messages land as intended.\n\nThis will help us refine A6 and later the summaries under T8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            36727,
            45096
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M13",
          "speaker_id": 45096,
          "reply_to": "M12",
          "text": "Yes, we can integrate a few short items on understanding of programme goals into the survey tools for A5.\n\nThat will also support the evaluation of inclusion aspects, for example whether students feel the programme is welcoming and fair.\n\nWe just need to keep the tools short so hotel staff and students are willing to complete them during a busy term.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T4",
            "T10"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            36727,
            497314

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M14",
          "speaker_id": 52968,
          "reply_to": "M6",
          "text": "Let me try to summarise what I am hearing so far and see if we can close on the pilot objective.\n\nProposed objective for the pilot: design and run a small-scale, inclusive hospitality internship in 2 to 3 hotels, where a mixed group of students complete a structured cycle of around 10 to 12 hours per week, with clear safeguards, no major operational incidents, and basic pre and post data collection to inform future scaling.\n\nIf you agree, I will treat this as our working objective and success criteria for D1 and reflect it in the draft framework for T2.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D1"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            36727,
            19278,
            72802,
            45096,
            497314
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M15",
          "speaker_id": 36727,
          "reply_to": "M14",
          "text": "This wording works for me. It gives us a clear target for A1 and later A5 without locking us into a rigid model.\n\nI will use this objective when framing the needs assessment questions for T1 so that we can test whether stakeholders see it as realistic and inclusive.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "T1",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D1"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            52968

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M16",
          "speaker_id": 19278,
          "reply_to": "M14",
          "text": "I am comfortable with that objective and success description as long as we keep the list of allowed tasks aligned with safety and guest expectations.\n\nFrom the hotel side, the key is that interns are supervised and not left alone with complex or risky duties. We can refine that in detail under T3 and T11, but the overall direction for D1 looks good.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T3",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D1"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            52968

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M17",
          "speaker_id": 72802,
          "reply_to": "M14",
          "text": "I agree with the proposed objective and success criteria.\n\nThe 10 to 12 hours per week range is manageable from an academic timetable perspective, and we can later translate that into credits or recognition in T9.\n\nSo from my side, D1 is fine as you phrased it.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D1"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            52968
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M18",
          "speaker_id": 497314,
          "reply_to": "M14",
          "text": "I am also on board with that objective.\n\nIt gives us a clear story to tell: a focused pilot in a few hotels, with clear safeguards and learning goals. That will help shape A6 and later the public-facing parts of A8.\n\nNo changes from my side for D1.",
          "artifact_refs": [

            52968

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M19",
          "speaker_id": 52968,
          "reply_to": "M9",
          "text": "On hotel selection for the pilot under T7, I hear two main points: focus on mid-size city hotels that already have some experience with trainees, and include at least one smaller independent hotel if possible.\n\nUnless there are objections, I suggest we define D2 as: target 2 to 3 hotels, primarily mid-size city hotels with prior trainee experience, plus one independent hotel if feasible.\n\nI will start mapping potential partners accordingly for T7 and share a shortlist before any formal outreach.",

            36727
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M20",
          "speaker_id": 19278,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "That definition for D2 works for me.\n\nWhen you have a draft list for T7, I can quickly flag which hotels are more likely to cope with interns without heavy disruption, based on their layout and staffing patterns.",

        {
          "msg_id": "M22",
          "speaker_id": 52968,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "As a follow-up to our kickoff, I am sharing a first outline for the internship programme framework that will become A2 and feed into T2.\n\nKey elements I am proposing:\n- Duration: 8 to 10 weeks, around 10 to 12 hours per week, aligned with what we discussed.\n- Roles: clear responsibilities for students, hotel supervisors, university coordinator, and policy contact.\n- Safeguards: compliance with education and labour rules, including working time, insurance, and non-discrimination.\n\nBefore I draft the full text for A2, I would like feedback on this structure and on how we should map activities to academic requirements for T9. Please share any concerns or additions, especially around safeguards and learning outcomes.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T2",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            72802,
            36727,
            45096,
            19278,
            497314
