          "reply_to": "M59",
          "text": "I will join the Day 2 window and handle the quick test runs after placement.\nIf we see any major issue, we will fall back to the manual backup station and not extend the move window without checking with production.",

          "reply_to": "M59",

          "reply_to": "M62",

          "speaker_id": 557389,

          "msg_id": "M71",
          "speaker_id": 558542,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "We completed the first pilot batch through the new cell and I have logged the results in the performance log A5 for T11.\nSummary:\n- Batch size: 40 units\n- Average cycle time per unit: about 9 minutes end-to-end\n- Stoppages: 3 short stops (tool change, minor adjustment), 1 longer stop (press sensor issue)\n- Defects: 3 PCB solder issues, 2 mechanical alignment issues, 1 failed final functional test.\nI would like your views on whether we address these with quick actions and proceed to full go-live, or run another pilot after adjustments.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            55482,
            557389,
            89646,
            49338,
            416835
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M72",
          "speaker_id": 89646,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "Looking at A5, the 3 PCB solder issues were:\n- 2 cold joints\n- 1 missing component.\nAll were caught at the PCB continuity and visual checks defined in T3 and A3, so they did not reach final test.\nI think we can reduce these by reinforcing the visual criteria and maybe adjusting the iron tip for better heat transfer.\nNo need to change the process flow, just tighten the standard work and training.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T3",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M73",
          "speaker_id": 49338,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "On the mechanical side, the 2 alignment issues in A5 came from:\n- One case of cables slightly pinched\n- One housing not fully seated.\nBoth were caught at the mechanical visual check and fixed before final test.\nI will stress the cable check and torque mark steps in T4 and the visual guide so operators slow down a bit on those points.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T4",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M74",
          "speaker_id": 55482,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "The longer stop in A5 was due to a press sensor not reading correctly.\nWe reset and adjusted it, but for T6 I will add a quick sensor function check to the daily checklist.\nI do not see a structural issue with the equipment, more a tuning and routine check item.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M75",
          "speaker_id": 557389,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "From my review of A5, the failed final functional test was a loose connector.\nIt slipped through mechanical but was caught at final test.\nWe re-seated it and the unit passed.\nI suggest we add a quick connector tug check at mechanical in T4 and highlight it in A3.\nThat should reduce this type of failure.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T4",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            49338,
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M76",
          "speaker_id": 416835,
          "reply_to": "M71",
          "text": "From a flow and staging view, the material routes defined in T5 worked fine.\nNo congestion in the aisles, and the U-shape in A1 felt natural.\nThe only small issue was some confusion about where to place rework units.\nMaybe we can mark the rework racks more clearly and mention them in the operator training notes A8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T5",
            "A1",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M77",
          "speaker_id": 558542,
          "reply_to": "M72",
          "text": "Thanks for the breakdown.\nOn cycle time, 9 minutes per unit is a bit above our target, but for a first pilot with stops and learning, it is not bad.\nIf we implement the quick fixes you all mentioned and reinforce training using A8 and the visual guides, I expect we can bring it down.\nQuestion to everyone: do you feel there are any major risks that would justify another full pilot before go-live, or can we proceed with a controlled ramp-up?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A8",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            55482,
            557389,
            89646,
            49338,
            416835
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M78",
          "speaker_id": 89646,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "From PCB side, I am comfortable proceeding.\nThe issues we saw are manageable with better focus on the existing checks in T3 and a short refresher using A3 and A8.\nNo need for a full extra pilot just for PCB.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T3",
            "A3",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M79",
          "speaker_id": 49338,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "Same here.\nMechanical issues were caught early and fixed.\nIf we update T4 with the extra connector tug check and emphasize cable routing in training, I think we can move to go-live with close monitoring of the first days.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T4",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558542
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M80",
          "speaker_id": 55482,
          "reply_to": "M77",
          "text": "From equipment side, I do not see a reason to delay.\nThe sensor issue is now on the daily checklist in T6, and the rest of the stops were minor.\nI would recommend we proceed to go-live but keep A5 active for the first few production days to track any new patterns.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T6",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [

          "msg_id": "M19",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Following up on the overall flow, here is an initial proposal for labeling and storage for staged orders for T2.\nLabel format:\n- Order ID\n- Customer name (initial plus last name)\n- Pickup date and time window\n- Number of packages (for example, 1 of 3)\n- Special handling icons (fragile, chilled, plants)\nStorage zoning:\n- Zone A: standard goods\n- Zone B: fragile and electronics\n- Zone C: bulky items staged by movers\n- Zone D: short-stay area near floral and bakery for sensitive items\nThis would be documented in A8 and referenced in A1.\nCan you check if these zones and label fields work from your sides?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A8",
            "A1",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128135,
            213765,
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M20",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "From the moving side, having a dedicated Zone C for bulky items is helpful.\nI would like to add that Zone C should be close to an entrance or a wide aisle so I can bring items in without blocking customers.\nFor the labels, could we add a simple code that tells me if I need to use a trolley or two-person lift, or is that too detailed for T3?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A8",
            "T3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M21",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "For documentation, I like that the label mirrors the fields in A2.\nIf we keep the order ID and customer name consistent between A2 and the physical label, it will be easier to find orders.\nI suggest we standardise the special handling icons based on A3 and A4, so we do not invent new symbols in each department.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M22",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "Zone D for sensitive items works, but for plants I would like to keep them in our area until close to pickup, as we said.\nMaybe we can say that Zone D is a virtual zone for floral and bakery, meaning the label is prepared and the order is marked as staged in A2, but the physical item stays with us until the last moment.\nIn T6 and A4 I can describe how we handle watering and light while they wait.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A2",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M23",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "From the office side, the label fields you propose line up well with what we plan in A2 for T5.\nI would only add a small barcode or QR code field if we can generate it from existing tools, but since we cannot buy new software, we might need to keep it manual for now.\nSo I support your current label fields as the base standard.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T5",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M24",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M20",
          "text": "Good point on the lift support.\nTo keep the label readable, how about we add a simple code like B for bulky and H for heavy, based on the handling rules in A3.\nWe can define those codes in T3 and list them in A8 so everyone understands them.\nThat way you know when to bring a trolley without overloading the label.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A8",
            "T3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128135,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M25",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M24",
          "text": "Yes, a simple B or H code is enough for me.\nIf we write in A3 that B means bulky and H means heavy, I will know what equipment to use.\nPlease also note in T2 that Zone C should have enough space for trolleys to turn.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M26",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "For plants, I will define in T6 that we tag them with the same label format but keep them on our benches.\nWhen the pickup window starts, we move them to the pickup point or Zone D.\nIn A4 I will also add icons for sun, shade, and fragile stems so movers and sales assistants know how to handle them.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            128135
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M27",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M24",
          "text": "On fragile and electronics in Zone B, I will make sure A3 includes clear packaging instructions, especially for TVs and audio equipment.\nWe should also note in A8 that Zone B shelves should not be overloaded and that boxes are stacked only up to a safe height.\nThis will help prevent damage before pickup.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A8",
            "T3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128135,
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M28",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M23",
          "text": "Given our constraint on tools, I agree we keep the label manual for now.\nI will align the fields in A2 so that order ID, customer name, pickup window, and special handling codes match exactly what you print on the label.\nThis will also make it easier to use A7 later when we log and resolve issues.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "A8",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M29",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M19",
          "text": "Let me recap the labeling and zoning approach so we can lock it in for T2 and A8:\n- Label fields: order ID, customer name (initial plus last name), pickup date and time window, package count, and special handling icons.\n- Codes: B for bulky, H for heavy, plus icons for fragile, chilled, and plants, aligned with A3 and A4.\n- Zones: A for standard goods, B for fragile and electronics, C for bulky items, D as a short-stay or virtual zone for floral and bakery.\nIf everyone is ok with this, I will treat it as our standard labeling and storage zoning approach.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D3"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            128135,
            213765,
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "The recap matches what I need.\nWith Zones B and C clearly defined, I can plan my route in T9 so that I move bulky and fragile items at set times.\nPlease just make sure A3 lists the B and H codes so I do not miss them on the labels.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T9",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M31",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "I am aligned with this.\nIn T6 and A4 I will describe how we keep plants in our area until pickup and then move them to Zone D.\nI will also use the same icons you mentioned so the labels are consistent.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M32",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "From the office side, I confirm that this labeling and zoning scheme works and I will reference it in A1 and A7 when we describe how to find and escalate issues with staged orders.\nIt will also help when we train staff using A6 and A8.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A6",
            "A7",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M33",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M29",
          "text": "With this agreed, I will make sure the handling rules in A3 and the staging checklist in A8 reference Zones A to D and the B and H codes.\nThis will also feed into the training checklist in T7 so everyone learns the same pattern.\nOn handling rules for fragile, bulky, and perishable items, I suggest we confirm that A3 and A4 will be our final reference for launch.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            128135,
            213765
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M34",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M33",
          "text": "I confirm that for movers we will follow A3 as the main reference for handling fragile, bulky, and perishable items.\nOnce you and the specialised sellers finalise A3 and A4, I will adjust my daily routine in T9 to match those rules.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            213765,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M33",
          "text": "From the floral and garden side, I agree that A4, aligned with A3, will be our final rule set for handling plants and similar items.\nI will make sure T6 is consistent with that and with the zones we defined.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M33",
          "text": "Then we can state that A3 and A4, together with A8, are our final handling rules for fragile, bulky, and perishable items for launch.\nI will update T2 to reference them explicitly so that the staging and labeling method is fully aligned.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D4"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            140484,

            213765
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M36",
          "text": "Great, I will cross-check A1 so that it points to A3, A4, and A8 for any handling questions.\nThis will also feed into A6 when we prepare the training sessions.",
          "artifact_refs": [

          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have a first draft of the order tracking sheet for T5 and the filing rules for T12 ready to review.\nFor A2, the sheet currently has these fields:\n- Order ID\n- Customer name\n- Contact details\n- Items summary\n- Status (New, In preparation, Staged, Ready for pickup, Picked up, Cancelled, Returned)\n- Pickup deadline\n- Storage zone (A, B, C, D)\n- Notes (for example, B or H code, special handling)\nFor T12, I propose we keep paper documents in a click-and-collect binder by date and store digital copies in a shared folder with subfolders by month.\nCan you check if these fields and the status codes cover your needs?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            27468,
            128135,
            213765
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Thanks for sharing.\nFrom my side, the status list looks good and matches the flow we agreed in A1.\nI would add one more status: Delayed, so we can track when we have informed the customer using A5.\nFor T12, we should also define a simple naming convention for digital files, maybe order ID plus date, to make retrieval easier.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A2",
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "From the sales floor, the key for us is being able to quickly see if an order is staged and where it is.\nThe Storage zone field and the Status field already cover that.\nCould we also have a simple flag or note when an order includes plants or bakery goods, so we know to coordinate with specialised sellers before promising a pickup time at the counter?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            213765,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M40",
          "text": "Yes, a flag for plants would help.\nMaybe we can use the same icons we defined for labels in A4 and A8 and just note them in the Notes field.\nIn T6 I can specify that when the plant icon is present, the sales assistant should check with us before confirming exact pickup time.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A8",
            "T6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            27468,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "For movers, I mainly need to see which orders are in Zone C or have B or H codes.\nIf the Storage zone and Notes fields show that, I can plan my runs.\nMaybe we can also add a simple time field for when the order should be moved to staging, so I do not move bulky items too early.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A3",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "Good call on the Delayed status.\nI will add it between Ready for pickup and Cancelled.\nFor T12, I like the idea of using order ID plus date as the file name.\nSo a digital file could be something like CC-OrderID-Date, stored in a monthly folder.\nWe can test retrieval of three sample orders as required in T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "On the time field for movers, we could add a column called Move by, which indicates the latest time the order should be in the staging area.\nThis would be filled by the office clerk when confirming the pickup window with the customer using A5.\nThat way your T9 planning can rely on A2 without extra messages.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A5",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128135,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "If we use the same icons in the Notes field, that should be enough for us.\nWhen I see the plant or bakery icon, I will check with the specialised seller before confirming a tight pickup window.\nWe can also include this in A7 as a common issue prevention tip.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "A7",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            213765,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Let me summarise the final field list for A2 and T5:\n- Order ID\n- Customer name\n- Contact details\n- Items summary\n- Status (New, In preparation, Staged, Ready for pickup, Delayed, Picked up, Cancelled, Returned)\n- Pickup deadline\n- Move by time\n- Storage zone (A, B, C, D)\n- Notes (B or H codes, plant or bakery icons, other remarks)\nIf everyone agrees, I will treat this as the approved structure and start testing with five mock orders.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            27468,
            128135,
            213765
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "This list works for me.\nWith the Move by time and Storage zone, I can plan my daily route in T9.\nPlease share the mock sheet once you have tested it so I can try a day of moves on paper.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T9"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 213765,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "I am fine with this structure.\nThe Notes field will be enough for us to mark plant-related details.\nIn T6 and A4 I will just make sure we describe how to use those icons consistently.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T6",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "From the sales floor, this setup will help us quickly check if an order is ready and where it is.\nPlease include a short explanation of the statuses and icons in A7 so new staff can look it up during busy times.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "On T12, we still need to confirm the archiving rules.\nI propose:\n- Paper: keep in a daily binder for 1 month at the counter, then move to monthly archive boxes for 12 months.\n- Digital: store in a shared click-and-collect folder, with subfolders by year and month, and keep for at least 2 years.\nThis should cover basic receipt retention without overloading storage.\nIf we agree, we can document this in A1 and A7 as the standard.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "A7",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "Your proposal sounds reasonable and fits with what we do for other documents.\nI will check with store management to confirm that the 12-month paper and 2-year digital retention meets our compliance expectations.\nAssuming they agree, I will write this into T12 and update A2 and A7 to reference the archive locations.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "A7",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "With the fields and statuses agreed and the archiving rules defined, we can say that A2 and T5 are approved for launch.\nI will help you run the test with five mock orders to make sure there is no data loss and that retrieval works as described in T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A2",
            "T5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [

          ],

          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 140484,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted the customer communication templates for T4 and the procedure for partial pickups, cancellations, and refunds for T8.\nFor A5, I prepared three main templates:\n1) Order confirmation: includes order ID, items summary, expected pickup window, and what documents to bring.\n2) Ready for pickup: confirms that the order is staged, where to go in the store, and the pickup deadline.\n3) Delay or issue notice: explains the delay, new expected time, and who to contact.\nFor T8, the exception procedure follows our existing POS rules for refunds.\nCan you review and suggest any changes before we ask store management to approve A5?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T4",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            403118,
            27468,
            128135,
            213765
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 403118,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "I reviewed your drafts.\nThe structure is clear.\nI would suggest we add a short note in the order confirmation about how we handle mixed orders with perishable or fragile items, so customers know they should pick them up within a shorter window.\nWe can base that on A3 and A4.\nFor T8, we should also mention that any refund must be processed through the existing POS flow, not manually.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "A4",
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 27468,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "From the counter perspective, it would help if the ready-for-pickup template clearly states the pickup point location and any time limits.\nThat way we can just repeat the same message in person.\nFor partial pickups, we need a simple step-by-step in T8 so that sales assistants know when to call the office clerk and when they can handle it directly at the counter.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 128135,
          "reply_to": "M53",
          "text": "For movers, the main impact is when there is a delay or a partial pickup.\nIf the delay notice in A5 includes a new Move by time, that will help me adjust my route.\nIn T8, please also note that if a bulky item is cancelled after staging, I need to know whether to move it back to storage or to a returns area.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A3",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            140484,
            403118
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",

          "text": "Thanks for pulling A2 together.\nFrom a leadership view, I want the checklist to be simple enough for on-site staff to use consistently, but also robust enough to protect us on compliance and disputes.\nPlease make sure:\n- we capture photos and meter readings clearly, as this links to T5 and the inventory in A4\n- the steps align with the service levels we plan to communicate to owners and tenants later\nOnce we converge on content, I will be looking to formally approve A2 for use in the pilot.",

          "speaker_id": 52814,

          "reply_to": "M22",
          "text": "On the contract side, I will align A2 with A3 and T4 by:\n- listing all documents that must be signed or acknowledged at move-in\n- adding a check that the signed agreement matches the approved template and agreed terms\n- including a step at move-out to confirm notice periods and any applicable penalties\nI will also flag in T9 that these points need to be reflected in the tenant FAQ.\nOnce I have incorporated all of this, I will ask you to do a quick review for any legal gaps.",

        {

          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M24",
          "text": "One more suggestion for A2: in the move-out section, add a step to check for any outstanding rent or charges and to inform tenants clearly about the timeline for deposit return.\nThis will reduce complaints and ties into the arrears tracking we will later show in the dashboard.\nIt also gives us a consistent script for staff when tenants move out.",

          "text": "Agree, and from a contract perspective that step should reference the clauses in A3 about deposit handling and arrears.\nWe should avoid staff improvising explanations.\nMaybe in A2 we can point to a short script or to the FAQ under T9, so everyone uses the same wording.",
          "artifact_refs": [

          "reply_to": "M31",
          "text": "Noted.\nWith confirmation from operations and on-site, I am approving A2 as the standard tenant onboarding and changeover checklist for the pilot.\nPlease make sure it is uploaded to the shared repository and communicated to staff in the pilot buildings.\nNow we need to close on A3 so that contracts are aligned with the checklist and the FAQ under T9.",

          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have drafted an initial proposal for the maintenance and inspection schedule in A5, based on the inventory data we are compiling in A4 under T5 and the operating model in A1.\nThis is part of T6.\nFor now, I have grouped buildings into three categories by type and age and suggested inspection frequencies and scope for each.\nI would like your input on:\n- whether the proposed frequencies are realistic and compliant\n- if the scope of each inspection is clear enough for on-site staff\n- how we should handle urgent issues versus planned preventive tasks\nOnce we agree, we can finalise A5 and align it with the compliance checklist in T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4",
            "A1",
            "T5",
            "T6",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424,
            54175,
            128593,
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Looking at A5, the monthly visual checks and annual full inspections for the newer buildings are fine.\nFor the older Riverside block, I would suggest we keep quarterly checks for common areas, as we already see more wear there.\nOn scope, it would help if A5 links directly to the compliance checklist from T12, so I know exactly what to look at for fire safety, access, ventilation, and energy items.\nThat way I can use one list on site instead of switching between documents.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "From a regulatory and risk angle, the frequencies in A5 need to align with the minimum requirements for fire safety and energy performance.\nFor example, some fire equipment checks must be done more often than the general building inspection.\nI recommend we:\n- use T12 as the baseline for mandatory items and mark them clearly in A5\n- distinguish between statutory checks and our own preventive checks\nThis will also help when we explain the schedule to owners and tenants later.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M41",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "Thanks for the draft.\nI want to make sure the schedule in A5 is both compliant and manageable for on-site staff.\nWe should avoid overloading 167424 with reporting that does not add value.\nPlease check that:\n- the inspection scope is clearly defined and linked to T12\n- urgent issues have a clear escalation path, consistent with the incident procedure we will define later\nOnce we have a stable proposal, I will sign off on the inspection frequencies and scope for each building category.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M42",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M39",
          "text": "Good point on Riverside.\nI will adjust A5 so that older blocks have quarterly common-area checks, while newer ones keep the monthly visual and annual full inspections.\nI will also link each inspection type in A5 to the relevant sections of the T12 checklist, so you can use one combined list on site.\nFor urgent issues, I suggest we treat them outside the regular schedule and route them through the incident procedure we will document in A8 and T11.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12",
            "A8",
            "T11"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "That works for me.\nIf A5 clearly marks which checks are statutory from T12 and which are extra, I can plan my time better.\nFor urgent issues, as long as the incident procedure in A8 allows me to act immediately on safety risks and then log them, we will be fine.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12",
            "A8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M44",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M42",
          "text": "When you update A5, please also:\n- mark the items in the schedule that are directly tied to legal requirements from T12\n- add a note where external certified contractors are needed, for example for certain fire systems or energy inspections\nThis will help avoid any confusion about who is allowed to perform which checks.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M44",
          "text": "Understood.\nI will revise A5 to:\n- differentiate statutory checks from additional preventive ones\n- flag items that require external certified contractors\n- link each inspection type to the relevant T12 checklist items\nOnce done, I will share the updated schedule for final review.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            128593,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "From an admin perspective, it would help if A5 also indicates how inspection results feed into A4 and later into the dashboard.\nFor example, a simple status field for each unit or building that we can update after each inspection.\nThat will make it easier to track open issues and inspection status without extra spreadsheets.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M46",
          "text": "Good idea.\nI will add a status field and a simple coding in A5 that can be mirrored in A4 and later in the dashboard template.\nThat way we can see at a glance which buildings are up to date on inspections and where there are outstanding issues.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M48",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M38",
          "text": "I have now updated A5 with:\n- adjusted frequencies for older versus newer buildings\n- clear links to T12 items and flags for statutory checks\n- notes on when external contractors are required\n- a status field that ties into A4\nPlease review this version and confirm if the inspection frequencies and scope per building category are acceptable.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424,
            128593,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M49",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "I have checked the updated A5.\nThe frequencies and scope look realistic, and the links to T12 make it clear what I need to check.\nFrom the on-site side, I am comfortable working with this schedule.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M50",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M48",
          "text": "I have reviewed the revised A5 against the regulatory checklist in T12.\nThe statutory items are correctly marked, and the proposed frequencies meet or exceed the minimum requirements.\nI do not see any compliance gaps.\nI recommend we approve this schedule for the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M51",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M50",
          "text": "Thanks for the thorough review.\nBased on the feedback, I am confirming the inspection frequency and scope per building category as defined in A5, and we will treat the T12 checklist items as mandatory for all buildings in the portfolio.\nThis will be our standard for the pilot and for future rollout, unless regulations change.\nPlease proceed with testing the checklist on at least one building as required by T12.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M52",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M51",
          "text": "I will coordinate with 167424 to apply the T12 checklist and the A5 schedule on one of the Oak Street buildings this week.\nWe will capture any practical issues and adjust wording if needed before full rollout.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A5",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M53",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M52",
          "text": "Confirmed.\nI will run through the T12 checklist on Oak Street Block A and log the results in A4, following the schedule in A5.\nI will share feedback on how long it takes and any unclear items.",
          "artifact_refs": [

          "msg_id": "M54",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "I have created a first version of the Property Performance Dashboard Template in A6 as part of T7.\nIt is a simple sheet for now, focused on the pilot buildings.\nCurrent metrics include:\n- occupancy rate\n- rent arrears\n- number of open maintenance issues\n- inspection status based on A5\n- average resolution time for incidents\nI would like your input on which KPIs we should keep, add, or remove, and how often we should update and share this with owners and senior management.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T7",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            48703,
            128593,
            167424
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M55",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "From an operations view, the metrics you listed in A6 are a good start.\nI would add:\n- number of tenant complaints and their status\n- percentage of units with up-to-date inventory and condition data from A4\nThese will help us see if the centralised model is improving tenant satisfaction and data quality.\nFor update frequency, I suggest we track most metrics monthly, but keep an internal weekly view on open issues and arrears during the pilot.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M56",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "I agree with the core KPIs in A6 and the additions suggested by 48703.\nI would also consider:\n- average time from application to move-in, to see if the new processes speed up leasing\n- percentage of contracts using the new A3 templates\nThese link directly to T4 and the tenant lifecycle work.\nFor owners, we should keep the view simple: occupancy, arrears, major incidents, and inspection compliance.\nMore detailed metrics can stay internal.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M57",
          "speaker_id": 167424,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "From the site side, it would help if the KPIs in A6 are easy to update.\nIf we keep it to a few fields I can update after inspections or incidents, that is fine.\nToo many detailed metrics might be hard to maintain.\nMaybe we can automate some of the data from A4 and A5 later.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4",
            "A5"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            48703
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M58",
          "speaker_id": 54175,
          "reply_to": "M54",
          "text": "For leadership and owners, I want the dashboard in A6 to answer three questions:\n- Are we full enough and collecting rent on time\n- Are we keeping buildings safe and in good condition\n- Are tenants satisfied and issues resolved quickly\nThe metrics proposed so far cover most of this.\nI would like us to agree on a final list of KPIs and then decide how often we share the summary with owners and senior management.\nMy initial thought is monthly for owners and monthly or quarterly for senior management, with ad-hoc updates if something material changes.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            52814,
            48703,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M59",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M55",
          "text": "I will update A6 to include:\n- tenant complaints count and status\n- percentage of units with up-to-date inventory data from A4\n- average time from application to move-in\n- percentage of contracts using A3 templates\nI will keep the owner-facing view limited to occupancy, arrears, major incidents, and inspection compliance, as suggested.\nWe can keep the more detailed metrics on a separate internal tab.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A4",
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            48703,
            128593
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M60",
          "speaker_id": 48703,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "On cadence, I support monthly reporting to owners, with a simple one-page summary from A6.\nFor senior management, a monthly view during the pilot makes sense so we can react quickly if something is off.\nAfter the pilot, we can move to quarterly if things are stable.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M61",
          "speaker_id": 128593,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "I agree with that cadence.\nMonthly updates to owners will also help manage expectations around inspections and any planned works.\nWe should align the reporting dates with the communication plan under T8 so that messages are consistent and not too frequent.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            54175,
            52814
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M62",
          "speaker_id": 52814,
          "reply_to": "M59",
          "text": "I have updated A6 with the new KPIs and separated the internal and owner views.\nCould you please check if the structure is clear and if any metric should still be removed or renamed before we lock it for the pilot",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6"
          ],

          "mentions": [

          "speaker_id": 166793,

The roadmap groups initiatives into three waves, with phase 1 aligned to the pilot properties we just approved under T6.           "text": "Looking at A3, the phase 1 list includes portal enhancements, basic energy dashboards, and digital notices. From an operations standpoint, portal enhancements and digital notices are manageable for the pilots, as long as we coordinate timing with local teams. The energy dashboards might require more coordination with facilities and suppliers, so I would prefer we limit that to one or two pilot buildings in phase 1. On A6, the messages are clear, but we need to be careful not to overwhelm tenants with too many changes at once.",

          "text": "From the financial and business case side, the initiatives in A3 look promising, but we need to be mindful of the budget envelope that will be set under T10. For phase 1, I would prioritise low dependency, low cost items that still show visible benefits, such as portal usability improvements and digital communication features.           "text": "From a quality and audit perspective, the digital initiatives in A3 can help with consistency if we design them well.           "text": "Understood.           "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "Thanks for pulling this together. A4 is comprehensive, but I am a bit concerned about the time it will take site teams to complete the full checklist during busy periods. For the pilots, I suggest we keep all safety related items mandatory, but consider grouping some of the service quality and sustainability checks into a lighter version for routine visits.           "speaker_id": 87909,
          "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "From a business and governance perspective, A4 is a good foundation, but we should be clear about which items are critical for compliance and which are more about continuous improvement. That will help us prioritise remediation actions in A7 and manage costs.           "text": "Looking at A4 and A7, I see a few points where digital tools from A3 and A6 could help. For example, we could use digital notices and portal messages to inform tenants about upcoming inspections or to follow up on incidents.           "reply_to": "M57",
          "text": "From my side, I want to ensure that the checklist in A4 is robust enough to satisfy regulators and our own standards, but not so heavy that it becomes a barrier to consistent use. On remediation, we should focus first on any safety or legal compliance gaps in A7, then on issues that strongly affect tenant experience. For T12, I would like a clear and simple process that we can explain to the board and to tenant representatives.",

          "speaker_id": 125632,
          "reply_to": "M58",
          "text": "That makes sense. I can adjust A4 so that safety items remain mandatory for every audit, while service quality and sustainability items are grouped into core and extended sections. For the pilots, we can use the full checklist during initial baseline audits under T8, and a lighter version for follow up visits.           "reply_to": "M62",

That will help when we compare with the food line cleaning and think about shared forklift routes.\nWe will also need to log the time per step in A4 once we pick the pilot machine.",

          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M7",
          "text": "Yes, I can break it down.\nTools:\n- Long-handled scraper for table and guides\n- Stiff brush for corners\n- Air gun for blade housing\n- Floor squeegee for oil spots\nFrequent chip buildup:\n- Under the infeed conveyor\n- Around the blade guard lower edge\n- In the floor expansion joints near the shared walkway\nI will document this in the T2 notes and estimate minutes per step so we can plug into A4 later.",

            "T2",
            "A4"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []

        {
          "msg_id": "M9",
          "speaker_id": 433963,
          "reply_to": "M2",
          "text": "For the food lines, we should also capture where we depend on other teams.\nExamples from my line:\n- Waiting for maintenance to unlock a guard that sticks\n- Waiting for QA to release after cleaning\n- Waiting for forklift to clear pallets\nIf we list these in T1 with rough wait times, A4 will show where the real downtime is, not just the washing itself.",

          "mentions": [
            102838

        {
          "msg_id": "M10",
          "speaker_id": 462838,
          "reply_to": "M5",
          "text": "I can sit with you next shift and help time each step.\nWe can write down:\n- Start and end time for each cleaning step\n- Any waiting time in between\nThen we can pass that to whoever is maintaining A4.\nThis will also complete part of T1 for our line.",

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            558848

        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M11",
          "speaker_id": 527555,
          "reply_to": "M1",
          "text": "To move forward we need to pick one food line and one metal saw as pilots.\nProposal:\n- Food pilot line: the cereal packing line where most of us rotate\n- Metal pilot machine: the main saw closest to the shared corridor\nThese seem to have the most interaction with forklifts and shared walkways, so they are good test cases.\nIf no one objects by tomorrow, we will log this as our pilot choice for D1 and start filling A4 for those two first.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T1",
            "T2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D1"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            310108,

            102838

        {
          "msg_id": "M12",
          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M11",
          "text": "From the metal side I am fine using the main saw by the corridor as the pilot.\nIt is the one that creates the most chips near shared traffic, so if we can keep that one under control the others will be easier.\nI will start tracking step times on that machine for A4 and complete T2 details there first.",

            "A4",

            "D1"

          "mentions": []

        {
          "msg_id": "M13",
          "speaker_id": 433963,
          "reply_to": "M11",
          "text": "Agree on using the cereal packing line as the food pilot.\nIt has frequent changeovers and we already know the main pain points.\nFor A4, I suggest we capture at least:\n- Start and end time for full cleaning and changeover\n- Time per main step\n- Waiting time by reason, like QA, forklift, maintenance\n- Any re-cleaning needed after restart\nIf everyone is ok with that, we can treat this as the base structure for D2.",

        {

          "speaker_id": 102838,

          "text": "The list for A4 makes sense to me.\nMaybe we also add who was on the shift, just initials, so if we see a big difference we can ask how they did it.\nI can start writing down times and reasons for waits on the cereal line next shift to help close T1.",

        {

          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M13",
          "text": "For the metal saw, I will mirror the same structure in A4:\n- Total cleaning time\n- Time per step\n- Waiting time, for example if we wait for chip bin to be emptied by forklift\n- Any rework if we find chips after restart\nThat way T2 and T1 data are comparable.\nI support using this as the agreed content for D2.",

          "text": "Summarizing for closure:\n- D1: Pilot assets will be the cereal packing food line and the main metal saw by the shared corridor.\n- D2: A4 will capture total time, time per step, waiting time with reason, re-cleaning events, and operator initials for both areas.\nNext step is to complete T1 and T2 mapping for those assets first, then extend to the other lines.",

          "msg_id": "M30",
          "speaker_id": 527555,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "We need to align on hygiene rules for forklifts and shared tools moving between food and metal zones.\nRight now there is no clear routine, and we have seen chips and dust near the food corridor.\nWe have a draft for the shared equipment checklist A3 under T4, but it needs input from both sides.\nLet us define the minimum cleaning steps before a forklift enters food areas and how often we log these checks.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            310108,
            102838,
            433963,
            462838,
            558848
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M31",
          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "From the metal side, the main risk is chips stuck on forklift wheels and forks.\nFor A3 I suggest minimum steps before entering food areas:\n- Visual check of wheels and forks\n- Brush off any visible chips from wheels, forks, and mast base\n- Quick wipe of forks if there is oil\nThis can be done in under 3 minutes if we keep a brush and rag at the crossing point.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M32",
          "speaker_id": 102838,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "On the food side, I would add a quick floor check where the forklift stops.\nSometimes chips fall when it brakes.\nMaybe A3 can include:\n- Check floor around stop point and sweep if needed\nAlso, for shared tools like brooms or shovels, we should not move them from metal to food without cleaning them first.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M33",
          "speaker_id": 462838,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "I am a bit unsure where we will keep the brush and rag for the forklift.\nIf it is too far, people will skip it.\nCould we add in A3 that cleaning tools must be stored at the gate between metal and food, so it is obvious and quick?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            527555
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M34",
          "speaker_id": 558848,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "For logging, I am worried that if we have to write too much, it will not happen.\nMaybe A3 can just have:\n- Time\n- Forklift ID\n- Tick box that wheels, forks, and floor were checked\nAnd we only log when entering the food area, not every move inside metal.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M35",
          "speaker_id": 433963,
          "reply_to": "M34",
          "text": "Agree, we should keep logging light.\nFor D6 we can say: log once per forklift per entry into the food zone, not every trip inside.\nA3 can be a small sheet near the gate with one line per entry.\nThat should keep it under 5 minutes as required in T4.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M36",
          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M32",
          "text": "On shared tools, I suggest we mark some tools as food-only and some as metal-only.\nFor tools that must be shared, A3 can require:\n- Brush or wipe tool to remove chips or food residue\n- Visual check before crossing the line between areas\nWe can also color-code handles so it is clear which tools stay where.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M37",
          "speaker_id": 527555,
          "reply_to": "M31",
          "text": "Putting this together for A3 under T4, the minimum steps before a forklift enters food areas could be:\n1. Visual check of wheels and forks\n2. Brush off visible chips from wheels, forks, and mast base\n3. Wipe forks if there is oil\n4. Check floor around stop point and sweep if needed\n5. Log entry on the small sheet with time, forklift ID, and tick box\nDoes everyone agree this is the right minimum for D5?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            310108,
            102838,
            433963
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M38",
          "speaker_id": 102838,
          "reply_to": "M37",
          "text": "Works for me.\nIf we keep the brush and broom right at the gate like mentioned, it should not slow us down much.\nI support using that list as the minimum steps for D5.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5"
          ],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M39",
          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M37",
          "text": "Agreed from metal side as well.\nThe sequence is practical and fits into the 3 to 5 minute window.\nWe just need to make sure the gate area has enough space to sweep safely.\nI also support logging once per entry as defined for D6.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M40",
          "speaker_id": 433963,
          "reply_to": "M30",
          "text": "To summarize and close:\n- D5: Before a forklift enters food areas, operators must follow the five-step check in A3: visual check, brush wheels and forks, wipe oily forks, sweep floor at stop point, and log the entry.\n- D6: Hygiene checks for forklifts are logged once per forklift per entry into the food zone on a simple sheet near the gate.\nT4 will now be updated so A3 reflects these rules and stays under 5 minutes to complete.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A3",
            "T4"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [
            "D5",
            "D6"
          ],
          "mentions": [
            527555,

          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "We are ready to start pilot runs for the new cleaning and changeover routines.\nAs agreed earlier, pilots will be on the cereal packing food line and the main metal saw by the shared corridor.\nWe need to confirm the pilot schedule, which shifts go first, and how we will record times in A4 while running T7 and T8.\nPlease share any constraints from your shifts before we lock the plan.",

          "speaker_id": 433963,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "For the food line, I suggest we start the pilot on the afternoon shift.\nMorning is usually packed with urgent orders, and we have less room for testing.\nAfternoon can run at least three full changeovers over two days without risking a long stop.\nI can take care of filling A4 for those runs under T7.",

          "mentions": []

        {
          "msg_id": "M43",
          "speaker_id": 102838,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "I am on the morning shift most days.\nIf we start with afternoon like suggested, I can join on day two to see how it works and then repeat the same steps on morning shift later.\nFor A4, do we need one sheet per changeover or can we log multiple runs on the same sheet?",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",

          "speaker_id": 527555,
          "reply_to": "M43",
          "text": "For the pilot under T7 and T8, let us use one line per changeover or cleaning cycle on A4.\nSo one sheet can hold several runs, but each run has its own row with start and end times and notes.\nThat will make it easier to compare the three pilot runs.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T7",
            "T8"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M45",
          "speaker_id": 310108,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "On the metal saw, the quietest window is usually late evening.\nI propose we run the three pilot cleaning cycles for T8 on the late shift over three consecutive days.\nThat way we can follow the full A2 checklist without pressure from urgent cuts.\nI will handle A4 entries for the saw during those runs.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A4",
            "T8",
            "A2"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": []
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M46",
          "speaker_id": 462838,
          "reply_to": "M41",
          "text": "For the food line, I just want to confirm we will not stop production for more than 2 hours.\nIf we follow A1 and the new steps, do we expect cleaning plus changeover to stay under that?\nI am ok to support on afternoon shift as long as we have that limit clear.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A1",
            "T7"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            433963
          ]
        },
        {
          "msg_id": "M47",

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.

ROLE INSTRUCTIONS
You are an EVALUATOR that infers latent behavioral signals from Slack-style corporate conversations.
You do NOT have access to the true scenario labels. You must infer using ONLY:
* trajectory_signature / the participant’s trajectory and summarized history (to calibrate vocabulary and context);
* the channel content and structure (messages + artifact_refs + decision_refs + thread_outcome).

CRITICAL OUTPUT RESTRICTIONS
* Return ONLY a single valid JSON object in the schema specified at the end.
* Do not include text outside the JSON.
* Do not use numbers (no score, no probability, no confidence).
* For each attribute, return ONLY one label in {LOW, MID, HIGH}.
* DETERMINISTIC RULE: if you are unsure/ambiguous, choose MID.
* Evidence snippets must be SHORT QUOTES from the text (no comments) and must NOT contain “LOW/MID/HIGH”.
* DO NOT use literal line breaks inside strings. If needed, use \n or if it is a tab use \t.
* Ensure quotes and braces are closed.

GLOSSARY (only for conceptual consistency; do NOT cite this in the output)
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions.

INPUT
* participants_json: list of participants, each with:
    {
        "_id": int,
        "role": string,                            # role of the participant
        "trajectory_lastK": [string],              # ESCO titles (short list, in chronological order)
        "trajectory_summary": string,              # consolidated summary (may contain “->”)
        "skills_text": string,                     # skills extracted from trajectory
    }
* channel: threads and messages (msg_id, speaker_id, reply_to, text, mentions, artifact_refs, decision_refs, reactions)
* (optional) thread_outcome per thread (decisions_made, next_steps)

IMPORTANT: You will use the participants' information [INPUT PARTICIPANTS] as a basis to try to infer the skill, productivity, and performance levels of each participant. Comparing the "resume/career path" with what can be observed in the "day-to-day" [INPUT CHANNEL] through the channel's messages. In other words, you can compare expectations (what is expected from the participant's career path and their position) with reality. Always evaluate participants in relation to the group, that is, within the group itself, who stands out the most, who stands out the least, and who is average, using the criteria of HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

ATTENTION: Within a given group/channel, it is possible for everyone to have the same classification — for example, all HIGH, all LOW, or all AVERAGE. It is also possible for them to be completely different, with each member having different labels. The fundamental requirement is that you classify each participant by mapping them according to OBSERVABLE signals. One detail (but not a rule) is that a participant usually has the same values/labels in more than one of their variables (ability, performance, and productivity). However, always classify based on evidence.

HOW TO MAP TO OBSERVABLE SIGNALS (do NOT cite this in the snippet; it is only an internal rule)
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)
* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates ok; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable precision.
* LOW: more initial misalignment; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, i.e., that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE:  “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates some of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, generally suggests that someone support them.

DETERMINISTIC PROCEDURE (for each participant)
1. Collect candidate evidence:
   * Messages where speaker_id == the participant’s _id.
   * If the participant speaks little, you can also use messages that mention them (mentions contains _id) as contextual evidence.
2. For each attribute (productivity, ability, performance), mark:
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of HIGH => candidate HIGH
   * 2 “in all threads there are strong signals” of LOW  => candidate LOW
   * otherwise => MID
3. Attention:
   * If there are strong signals of HIGH and LOW at the same time for the same attribute, choose MID (conservative rule).
   * In the corporate context, everyone needs to deliver and demonstrate work; be careful to infer HIGH for something standard that should be MID.
   * Having one to four pieces of evidence for threads (<= 4 evidence items * threads) is not strong evidence.
4. Little evidence:
   * If there are no messages from the participant, use MID for all three attributes and use evidence from a message where they were mentioned.

          "msg_id": "M67",
          "speaker_id": 53841,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "We have completed the initial pilot period for Cross-Plant Predictive Maintenance Rollout for Production Lines.\nI have drafted the Pilot Implementation and Lessons Learned Report (A7) based on data from the Pilot KPI and Downtime Tracking Sheet (A6) and the inputs to T10 and T12.\nHeadline results:\n- Unplanned downtime on pilot assets reduced by around 18 percent vs baseline.\n- MTBF improved on the forming press and case packer; smaller change on the palletizer.\n- Maintenance task completion rate improved but still below our long-term target.\nIn this thread, we need to:\n- Review the results and customer impact.\n- Decide whether to keep or adjust the pilot asset scope for scale-up (D1 revisit).\n- Confirm long-term ownership of alert triage and escalation (D4 revisit).\nPlease review A6, A7, and the draft Cross-Functional Rollout Roadmap (A8), then share your views.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "A6",
            "A7",
            "A8",
            "T10",
            "T12"
          ],
          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [

          "msg_id": "M68",
          "speaker_id": 36422,
          "reply_to": "M67",
          "text": "I went through A6 and A7.\nFrom an operations perspective, the forming press and case packer clearly delivered value; we saw fewer disruptive stops and more predictable maintenance.\nThe palletizer shows some improvement, but less pronounced, partly because one signal was deferred.\nFor D1, I would keep the current asset set for the next phase and add the deferred palletizer signal when we have a window, but I would not expand to additional assets yet.\nOn D4, the current ownership model worked reasonably well, though line supervisors needed some coaching on triage early on.",

          "speaker_id": 429831,
          "reply_to": null,
          "text": "Sharing a quick summary from the one-week dry run under T10. We delivered to 6 households across two routes. Overall, the flow worked, but we logged a few issues in A7: 1) On Route A, one parcel had an item close to its expiry date that should have been filtered out earlier. 2) On Route B, we had one missed delivery because the household was not in; chilled items were brought back as per A2. 3) A couple of staff reported that the doorstep script from A4 sometimes stretched beyond the planned 5 minutes when people wanted to talk. Let us use this thread to capture observations and agree what to adjust before the full 6-week roll-out.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T10",
            "A7",
            "A2",
            "A4"

          "decision_refs": [],
          "mentions": [
            516425,

        {
          "msg_id": "M71",
          "speaker_id": 516425,
          "reply_to": "M70",
          "text": "From the delivery side, both routes felt manageable, but the timing was tight when two households wanted longer conversations. For T11, I noted in A6 that the average doorstep time was closer to 7 minutes on Route B. One idea is to build a slightly larger buffer into T4, or to be clearer in the script about keeping the visit short while still being warm.",
          "artifact_refs": [
            "T11",
            "A6",
            "T4",
            "A4"

          "mentions": [
            429831
